author: chav-aniket
body:
## Summary
- Add 12 Zaidan-style UI component primitives (Button, Input, Label, Card, Badge, Dialog, Popover, Tabs, RadioGroup, Checkbox, Textarea, Avatar) to `@osn/ui` backed by Kobalte headless primitives
- Install `@kobalte/core`, `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge` as deps of `@osn/ui`
- Create `cn()` utility (clsx + tailwind-merge) as the shared class composition function
- Migrate `Register.tsx` and `SignIn.tsx` auth components to use Button, Input, Label
- Migrate all 11 `@pulse/app` components and 2 pages from inline Tailwind patterns to shared Zaidan components
- Add `--popover`, `--accent`, `--destructive-foreground` CSS variables to the theme
- Add new tests: `cn()` unit tests, InfoPopover (Kobalte Popover), CreateEventForm RadioGroup/Checkbox onChange
- Add `wiki/architecture/component-library.md` documenting the full Zaidan setup, patterns, and performance guidelines

## Workspaces affected
- `@osn/ui` (minor) — new deps, 12 new component files, `cn()` utility, updated auth components
- `@pulse/app` (patch) — consumer migration, CSS theme variables, updated tests

## Decisions & issues

**[Kobalte Tabs vs manual tabs in SignIn]** — conditional tab rendering
- **Issue:** Kobalte Tabs doesn't handle conditionally-rendered triggers well — when the Passkey tab appears after `onMount` (feature detection), Kobalte's internal state defaults to the first available tab instead of respecting the controlled `value` prop.
- **Why:** All 8 SignIn tests failed because the passkey form never rendered.
- **Solution:** Reverted to manual styled buttons with `role="tab"` and `aria-selected` for the SignIn method selector, using `cn()` for conditional styling. Kobalte Tabs is still used in RsvpModal where all triggers are present at mount time.
- **Rationale:** The SignIn form has dynamic tab visibility (passkey only shows when WebAuthn is supported), which is fundamentally incompatible with Kobalte's tab management. Manual tabs preserve full accessibility semantics and test compatibility.

**[P-W1]** — `tailwind-merge` adds ~12-14 KB to initial bundle
- **Issue:** `tailwind-merge` is a runtime dependency of every `cn()` call, adding to the critical path bundle for all routes.
- **Why:** Previously, class strings were static literals with zero runtime cost.
- **Solution:** Accepted for design-system ergonomics. Documented build-time evaluation options (Vite plugin, `tw-merge-plugin`, drop to `clsx`-only) in the component library wiki and added to Deferred Decisions in TODO.md.
- **Rationale:** ~15 KB is bounded and proportional to the benefit. Kobalte subpath imports are tree-shake friendly, limiting total new bundle to the primitives actually used.

**[P-W2]** — `cn()` replaces `classList` fine-grained reactivity
- **Issue:** SignIn tab buttons previously used SolidJS `classList` (fine-grained DOM updates). `cn()` recomputes the full class string on signal changes.
- **Why:** `classList` only mutates specific classes; `cn()` replaces the entire `className`.
- **Solution:** Documented in component library wiki that `classList` should be preferred inside `<For>` loops. No change needed for current usage (3 static buttons).
- **Rationale:** Undetectable at this scale. The guidance prevents pattern propagation into hot paths.

**[P-I1]** — `tabs.filter()` inline in RsvpModal JSX
- **Issue:** Creates a new array reference on every render, causing `<For>` to diff unnecessarily.
- **Why:** Pre-existing pattern, not introduced by this PR.
- **Solution:** Documented `createMemo` recommendation in component library wiki. No change — 4-element array filtering is negligible.
- **Rationale:** Not a regression; noted for future reference.

**[T-M1]** — InfoPopover had no test file
- **Issue:** InfoPopover was rewritten from manual event listeners to Kobalte Popover with no test coverage.
- **Why:** The old hand-rolled dismiss logic was replaced with Kobalte's built-in handling — misconfiguration (e.g., `onOpenAutoFocus`) would silently degrade all 6 help tooltips in the create-event form.
- **Solution:** Added `InfoPopover.test.tsx` covering trigger rendering, content visibility, toggle, and Escape dismissal.
- **Rationale:** Only Kobalte Popover consumer in the app — critical to verify the integration works.

**[T-U1]** — CreateEventForm RadioGroup/Checkbox onChange not directly tested
- **Issue:** Tests only verified form submission payloads, not that Kobalte RadioGroup/Checkbox onChange handlers update state correctly.
- **Why:** If Kobalte's onChange fires with an unexpected value type, the form state could silently hold wrong values.
- **Solution:** Added 3 tests: RadioGroup visibility change, RadioGroup join policy change, Checkbox SMS channel toggle — each verifies the value propagates to the submit payload.
- **Rationale:** End-to-end path now covered from click → state update → submit payload.

**[T-S1]** — `cn()` utility had no unit test
- **Issue:** Foundational utility used by every component had no direct test.
- **Why:** Misconfiguration would silently break class output across all components.
- **Solution:** Added 7 tests covering class joining, falsy filtering, Tailwind conflict resolution, conditional objects, and deduplication.
- **Rationale:** Quick, high-signal — validates plumbing and serves as documentation.

**[Security review]** — No findings
- **Issue:** N/A — clean UI refactoring with no security-relevant changes.
- **Why:** All form logic, auth flows, data handling, and API interactions remain identical.
- **Solution:** No action required.
- **Rationale:** New dependencies (@kobalte/core, CVA, clsx, tailwind-merge) are well-known, widely-used packages appropriate for the SolidJS/Tailwind stack.

## Test plan
- [ ] `bun run --cwd osn/ui test:run` — 33 tests (4 files) pass
- [ ] `bun run --cwd pulse/app test:run` — 137 tests (13 files) pass
- [ ] `bun run check` — all 16 workspaces type-check clean
- [ ] `bun run lint` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- [ ] `bun run fmt:check` — all files formatted
- [ ] Verify Register flow renders correctly (email → handle → OTP → passkey)
- [ ] Verify SignIn tabs switch between Passkey / Code / Magic link
- [ ] Verify Create Event form RadioGroups and Checkboxes update correctly
- [ ] Verify RsvpModal opens as Kobalte Dialog with proper focus trap and Escape dismiss
- [ ] Verify InfoPopover shows/hides on click with proper positioning

author: copilot
body:
Gunicorn's default 30s (previously bumped to 120s) worker timeout was insufficient for Anthropic API calls during file uploads, memory compression, and large-context chats — causing `WORKER TIMEOUT` kills and HTML 500s returned to the client.

## Changes

- **`Procfile`** — `--timeout 120` → `--timeout 180`, added `--graceful-timeout 200`
- **`nixpacks.toml`** — expanded bare `gunicorn api.server:app --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT` to the full options set, matching the Procfile

```
gunicorn api.server:app \
  --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT \
  --workers 1 --worker-class sync \
  --timeout 180 --graceful-timeout 200 \
  --keep-alive 5 --log-level info
```

`graceful-timeout 200` (> `timeout 180`) ensures in-flight requests can finish before a worker is forcefully killed during rolling redeploys.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

The application is experiencing worker timeout crashes when handling AI API requests that take longer than 30 seconds. The logs show:

```
[2026-04-13 21:37:00 +0000] [1] [CRITICAL] WORKER TIMEOUT (pid:2)
[2026-04-13 21:37:00 +0000] [2] [ERROR] Error handling request POST /api/chat
```

The stack traces show the worker is being killed while waiting for responses from the Anthropic API (`api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`), particularly during operations like:
- Memory compression and summarization
- Chat message processing
- File uploads with AI analysis

## Root Cause

Gunicorn's default worker timeout is 30 seconds, which is insufficient for:
1. Claude API calls that can take 20-30+ seconds
2. Memory snapshot operations that make additional AI calls
3. File processing with large context

## Solution

Increase Gunicorn's timeout configuration to allow for longer-running AI operations:

1. **Add timeout configuration** to the Gunicorn startup command
   - Increase `--timeout` to 180 seconds (3 minutes) for AI operations
   - Set `--graceful-timeout` to 200 seconds to allow clean shutdown

author: keeb
body:
## Summary

Fixes [#108](https://github.com/systeminit/swamp/issues/108) — interactive `swamp data gc` silently skipped version-count GC when no lifetime-expired data existed, so resources with `lifetime: infinite, gc: N` accumulated unbounded versions. `--dry-run` under-reported the same work. Only `--force` and `--json` executed correctly.

**Root cause.** `dataGcPreview` surfaced only lifetime-expired entries via `findExpiredData`, and the CLI early-returned on an empty preview. Phase 2 version GC (`collectGarbage`) lived inside `deleteExpiredData` and was skipped entirely. Separately, the Phase 2 loop was gated on `if (!dryRun)`, so `--dry-run` never reported version GC counts.

**Fix.** Extend `UnifiedDataRepository.collectGarbage` with an optional `{ dryRun }` option that computes would-be counts without deleting. Expose it via a new `DataLifecycleService.previewVersionGarbage` method and aggregate it into `DataGcPreview.versionGcItems`. Widen the CLI early-return to check both categories. Remove the `if (!dryRun)` guard in `deleteExpiredData`, passing `dryRun` through to `collectGarbage` so `--dry-run` reports faithfully.

**Cleanup.** Consolidate two identical `parseDuration` copies into `src/domain/data/duration.ts`. (The grammar exists in four other places; deliberately out of scope for this PR.)

## Design

- **Repository-layer dry-run** was chosen over a parallel detection method so preview counts can never drift from actual pruning — there is exactly one source of truth for what gets removed.
- `DataGcPreview` grows additively (`items` field preserved) so downstream consumers keep working.
- `collectGarbage`'s options arg is optional, so all `() =>` stubs in model/driver/validation tests continue to satisfy the interface without changes.

## Test Plan

- [x] `deno check` — clean
- [x] `deno lint` — clean (1033 files)
- [x] `deno fmt --check` — clean (1047 files)
- [x] `deno run test` — 4345 passed, 0 failed
- [x] New unit tests: `duration_test.ts`; `previewVersionGarbage` + dry-run pass-through in `data_lifecycle_service_test.ts`; aggregation in `gc_test.ts`; renderer output in new `data_gc_test.ts`
- [x] New integration test: `collectGarbage` dry-run in `data_versioning_test.ts`
- [x] Manual reproduction at `/tmp/swamp-repro-issue-108` (12 versions at gc=10):
  - Interactive path: preview surfaces "version gc: 1 models with 12 excess versions", confirms, prunes 13 → 10
  - `--dry-run --json`: reports `versionsDeleted: 12` (was 0 before fix), no deletion
  - `--force`: prunes correctly, no regression
  - Empty repo: still shows "Nothing to clean up."

## Follow-ups

- File UAT coverage in `systeminit/swamp-uat` for `tests/cli/data/gc_test.ts` (interactive + `--dry-run`) plus an adversarial test for large version counts (>10k versions on a single model).

author: tmaxtor
body:
**Hi! Nice to meet you! A curious Abaper here :)** 
This is my first collaboration to a project and I hope this could be useful.

## Summary

This PR adds proper support for running the MCP server on SAP BTP ABAP Trial systems, where you can’t use a regular username/password and have to go through OAuth2 instead.

The server already worked nicely with on‑premise ABAP setups, but BTP Trial environments only accept OAuth2 tokens from the SAP UAA service. The whole idea behind this change was to make it easier to use the server for learning and experimenting on a personal BTP Trial account — which is exactly how a lot of developers get started with AI‑assisted ABAP development.

### Changes

#### New: Interactive PKCE login (`src/auth/login.ts`)

- `npm run login` launches a browser-based OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE flow against the SAP UAA endpoint.
- On success, tokens are saved to `.btp-tokens.json` (gitignored).
- Works on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

#### New: Token resolver with auto-refresh (`src/auth/oauth.ts`)

- `getToken()` is passed as `bearerFetcher` to `ADTClient`.
- Priority order: (1) valid stored user token → (2) refresh via `refresh_token` → (3) fallback to `client_credentials` grant (machine-to-machine, limited scope).
- This keeps the server running unattended without requiring re-login on every restart.

#### Modified: `src/index.ts`

- Replaced `SAP_USER` / `SAP_PASSWORD` with a `bearerFetcher` function passed to `ADTClient`.
- `SAP_USER` and `SAP_PASSWORD` are no longer required environment variables.
- Fixed a quirk in `abap-adt-api`'s internal validation: `ADTClient` requires a non-empty `username` even when OAuth2 is used. A placeholder value (`'oauth'`) is passed when `SAP_USER` is not set — it is never sent to the SAP server in bearer token mode.

#### Fixed: Logger stderr pollution

- `src/lib/logger.ts` was routing some output through `console.log` (stdout), which corrupts the MCP stdio stream. All log output now correctly goes to `console.error` (stderr).

#### Fixed: Double-wrapped JSON responses

- `serializeResult()` now detects when a handler already returns a `{ content: [...] }` envelope and passes it through as-is, preventing double serialization.

#### Updated: `.env.example`

- Replaced `SAP_USER` / `SAP_PASSWORD` with the BTP-specific variables: `SAP_TOKEN_URL`, `SAP_CLIENT_ID`, `SAP_CLIENT_SECRET`.
- Added optional `BTP_SERVICE_KEY_PATH` as an alternative to individual variables (points to the JSON service key downloaded from the BTP Cockpit).

**Feel free to take a look, and if you have suggestions, we can go through them together.**

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces multi-instance support for Proxmox and Docker services, allowing users to configure and manage multiple instances of each service type through the web UI settings panel. Previously, only a single instance per service (configured via environment variables) was supported.

## Key Changes

### Backend API
- **New endpoints** for service instance CRUD operations:
  - `GET /api/settings/instances` - List all configured instances
  - `POST /api/settings/instances` - Create a new instance
  - `PUT /api/settings/instances/{id}` - Update an instance
  - `DELETE /api/settings/instances/{id}` - Delete an instance
  - `POST /api/settings/instances/{id}/test` - Test instance connectivity

- **Database schema** - Added `service_instances` table to store instance configurations with JSON config blobs

- **Secret masking** - Instance configs with sensitive values (e.g., `token_value`) are masked as `••••••••` in API responses; masked values are preserved during updates to prevent accidental overwrites

### Integration Updates
- **Proxmox** (`proxmox.py`):
  - Refactored client creation into `_make_client()` for reusability
  - Added `_fetch_instance()` to fetch data from a single Proxmox instance
  - Added `_fetch_additional_instance()` to fetch data from DB-stored instances
  - Added `fetch_all_proxmox_data()` to aggregate default + additional instances
  - Updated cache keys to distinguish between instances (`proxmox:default`, `proxmox:{id}`)

- **Docker** (`docker_int.py`):
  - Refactored container fetching into `_fetch_containers()` for reusability
  - Added `_get_remote_client()` to connect to remote Docker hosts
  - Added `_fetch_additional_instance()` to fetch data from DB-stored instances
  - Added `fetch_all_docker_data()` to aggregate default + additional instances
  - Updated cache keys similarly (`docker:default`, `docker:{id}`)

### Frontend UI
- **Settings panel** now displays instance management cards for Proxmox and Docker:
  - View, edit, and delete existing instances
  - Add new instances with a form overlay
  - Save/test/delete buttons for each instance
  - Instance names and configuration fields are editable

- **Dashboard display** updated to show multi-instance data:
  - Proxmox and Docker sections now display grouped instances with headers
  - Instance-specific error states and status badges
  - Links to open Proxmox/Docker web UIs (when configured)
  - Docker container cards now include direct links to services based on mapped ports

### Configuration
- Added `DOCKER_URL` environment variable for Docker container web link generation
- Updated `.env.example` with Docker configuration example

### Testing
- Added comprehensive test suite (`test_instances.py`) covering:
  - CRUD operations for instances
  - Validation of service types and required fields
  - Secret masking and preservation during updates
  - Admin-only access control
  - Instance connectivity testing

## Implementation Details
- Instance configs are stored as JSON in the database and parsed/masked on retrieval
- The default instance (from env vars) is treated as a special case and aggregated with additional instances
- Caching is per-instance to allow independent refresh rates
- All instance operations require admin authentication
- The UI gracefully handles both single and multi-instance scenarios with appropriate grouping and headers

author: kmiller68
body:
#### bcd47e7f3fe74e08bd65657cdf5200ddd077e46f 
Add wasm wide arithmetic proposal
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=312213
rdar://174700268

Reviewed by Yusuke Suzuki.

Implement the WebAssembly wide-arithmetic proposal which adds four new
instructions behind the --useWasmWideArithmetic flag: i64.add128,
i64.sub128, i64.mul_wide_s, and i64.mul_wide_u. These operate on pairs
of i64 values to produce 128-bit results, encoded in the 0xFC prefix
space (extendedOps 19-22).

All three tiers are supported: IPInt uses new offlineasm instructions
(addqs/subqs/adcq/sbcq/smulhq/umulhq) to implement the operations
directly, BBQ uses platform-specific register-register sequences with
aliasing guards, and OMG lowers to patchpoints with appropriate register
constraints.

On x86_64, add128/sub128 use add+adc / sub+sbb pairs. mul_wide uses
single-operand mul/imul with rdx:rax output, with eax/edx clobbered
between consume and allocate to avoid conflicts with the BBQ register
allocator. On ARM64, add128/sub128 use adds+adc / subs+sbc, and
mul_wide uses umulh/smulh+mul pairs.

Also add an offset parameter to BBQJIT::topValue() so multi-result
operations can name their stack slots without manually computing the
base index. Use this in the wide arithmetic ops and in
returnValuesFromCall.

author: braydenpb
body:
## Summary

Add HTML entity decoding to pack hub API responses to properly display user-provided text (titles, descriptions, author names, tags, and addon names/notes). The server stores text with HTML entities encoded as a defense-in-depth measure against stored XSS, but since React already escapes text nodes on render, the encoded entities were displaying literally to users (e.g., `Spike's` instead of `Spike's`).

This change introduces a `decodeHtmlEntities` utility function that reverses the server's `escapeHtml` encoding by decoding only the five entities the server produces (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`), matching the server's allow-list exactly. The function is then applied to all user-provided text fields in the pack hydration pipeline.

The decoding order (ampersand last) ensures that double-escaped entities survive a round-trip correctly, maintaining alignment with the server's escaping behavior.

## Summary

Eliminates the sole remaining axiom from `LawOfSinesOQ06.lean`, completing the formalization of the Law of Sines with **0 axioms, 0 sorries**.

### Problem: law-of-cosines-oq-06

Previous state: 1 axiom (`sin_angle_mul_norms`), 0 sorries  
**New state: 0 axioms, 0 sorries**

### Proof

The axiom `sin(angle u v) * (‖u‖ * ‖v‖) = |cross2D u v|` is proved via Mathlib:

```lean
rw [InnerProductGeometry.sin_angle_mul_norm_mul_norm]
-- Goal: √(⟪u,u⟫·⟪v,v⟫ - ⟪u,v⟫·⟪u,v⟫) = |cross2D u v|
-- real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq + lagrange_2d → RHS = (cross2D u v)²
-- sqrt_sq_eq_abs closes the goal
```

Key dependency: `InnerProductGeometry.sin_angle_mul_norm_mul_norm` from `Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.Basic` (also fixes incorrect import `Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Angle`).

author: j0sh
body:
Record queues are wired in at graph build time and accumulate frames from session start. When recording begins later, the queue may already contain a backlog of stale frames from earlier in the session, causing the recorded content to span more source time than the actual recording wall-clock duration.

Flush the queue in RecordingCoordinator.start_recording() before constructing the QueueVideoTrack so recordings begin from "now."

Added test_recording_coordinator.py with a regression test verifying stale frames are drained before the recording track is initialized.

author: carbonscott
body:
## Summary

Restructure `xpm-seq-skills` to bundle everything needed to run `xpm-seq` inside a single git-clone-able directory, mirroring [`carbonscott/skill-docs-search`](https://github.com/carbonscott/skill-docs-search).

Before this PR, the skill repo only carried `SKILL.md` + `references/`, so any deployment had to manually fetch `xpm-seq.py` from `carbonscott/xpm-seq-tools`, hand-write a wrapper, and patch `SKILL.md` for shared use. After this PR, deployment is one command:

\`\`\`bash
# Claude Code
git clone https://github.com/carbonscott/xpm-seq-skills.git ~/.claude/skills/xpm-seq

# OpenCode
git clone https://github.com/carbonscott/xpm-seq-skills.git "\$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/xpm-seq"
\`\`\`

## What's added

- `bin/xpm-seq.py` — vendored from [`xpm-seq-tools@7706d60e`](https://github.com/carbonscott/xpm-seq-tools/commit/7706d60e), the single-file PEP 723 CLI
- `bin/xpm-seq` — 3-line bash wrapper that `exec`s `uv run --script bin/xpm-seq.py "\$@"`
- `env.sh` — adds `\$SKILL_DIR/bin` to `PATH`, sets `UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache-\$USER`, sources optional `env.local`
- `.gitignore` — hides `env.local`
- `README.md` — install / verify / standalone usage / layout / update workflow

## What's changed in SKILL.md

- Replace the upstream "Verify \`xpm-seq.py\` is in CWD" Step 1 with an "Environment Setup" section that sources \`env.sh\` (matches skill-docs-search wording).
- Rewrite every \`uv run --script xpm-seq.py <subcommand>\` example to plain \`xpm-seq <subcommand>\` — the wrapper handles \`uv run --script\` transparently once \`bin/\` is on \`PATH\`.
- Update the Step 7 error-recovery row from \`xpm-seq.py: No such file or directory\` to \`xpm-seq: command not found\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`source env.sh && xpm-seq ratecalc 100 --json\` returns valid JSON on macOS
- [x] PEP 723 cold-start resolves \`numpy\` on first run (~8 s)
- [x] \`bin/xpm-seq\` and \`bin/xpm-seq.py\` are mode 755
- [ ] Reviewer to verify on a Linux box (will be tested via SDF deployment immediately after merge)

## Updating the vendored script

When \`xpm-seq-tools\` ships a new pinned commit, re-vendor \`bin/xpm-seq.py\` and bump the SHA in \`README.md\`. No other files need to change.

### Motivation

- Replace the simplistic SQLite cookie-based auth with a hardened Postgres-backed auth system supporting RBAC, session revocation and credential lifecycle controls.
- Improve API safety by adding request size limits, rate limiting for auth/sensitive endpoints, strict security headers and optional HTTPS enforcement in production.
- Enforce stronger password policies, add MFA and admin user management to meet Phase 3/4 security requirements.
- Store mobile session tokens securely on-device using platform secure storage instead of plaintext `shared_preferences`.

### Description

- Introduced new and updated configuration options in `backend_fastapi/app/config.py` and `.env.example` (per-environment secrets, cookie samesite, request size limits, rate limit params, password policy and lockout settings).
- Reworked authentication in `backend_fastapi/app/auth.py` to use Postgres tables (`users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `auth_sessions`, `password_reset_tokens`, etc.), seeded RBAC and bootstrap admin, added TOTP-based MFA, password change/reset flows, session issuance/revocation, audit logging and many admin APIs for user/role management.
- Updated `backend_fastapi/app/main.py` to validate runtime security at startup, run DB-backed auth initialization, and add middleware enforcing content-length limits, per-IP rate limiting for login/sensitive endpoints, HTTPS enforcement in prod, and security response headers. Also registered many new `/auth/*` endpoints that exercise the auth subsystem.
- Added unit tests under `backend_fastapi/tests/test_auth_security.py` that validate password policy, runtime security checks and TOTP helpers, and added test package init.
- Added `lib/core/security/session_secure_storage.dart` and bumped `pubspec.yaml` to include `flutter_secure_storage` to securely persist session token and expiry on mobile; updated top-level README to document mobile security recommendations.
- Minor additions: package root `backend_fastapi/__init__.py`, docs (`docs/REVIEW_PROGRAMA_2026-04-13.md`), and README expansions describing RBAC, hardening and bootstrap guidance.

### Testing

author: kathishah
body:
## Summary

Implements full Step Functions skip routing so that reprocessing from a mid-pipeline step skips the preceding stages instead of re-running them. Verified across four testing layers.

### What changed

**Core pipeline change**
- `infra/infra/sundayalbum_stack.py` — replaces the single-Lambda `SkipLoad`/`SkipNormalize` approach with CDK `Choice` states. Each pre-split step (`Load`, `Normalize`, `PageDetect`, `Perspective`, `PhotoDetect`, `PhotoSplit`) and each per-photo step (`AiOrient`, `GlareRemove`, `Geometry`, `ColorRestore`) now routes to a `{Step}Skipped` Pass state when `start_from` is set and the current step index is below the requested start.
- `api/jobs.py` — `reprocess_photo_index` is always included in the SFN execution input (defaulting to `null`) so the Map state's `item_selector` JSONPath never raises `States.Runtime`.
- `handlers/common.py` and all step handlers — `start_from` skip logic removed from Lambda code (now owned entirely by SFN Choice states).

**Testing — 4 layers**
- **Layer 1 (unit, ≈85 tests):** `tests/handlers/test_handlers.py` — per-handler skip assertions via moto
- **Layer 2 (CDK template, 45 tests):** `infra/tests/unit/test_sfn_routing.py` — synthesises the stack in-process and asserts Choice conditions, Pass state existence, and exact `StringEquals` values
- **Layer 3 (Playwright UI, 5 tests):** `web/tests/e2e/sfn_ui.spec.ts` — manually triggered; verifies library donut segment count, `animate-ping` on the active step row, Load row availability, and single-photo reprocess photo isolation
- **Layer 4 (live SFN smoke, 3 tests):** `web/tests/e2e/sfn_smoke.spec.ts` — manually triggered; asserts `TaskStateEntered`/`PassStateEntered` events in execution history against the live dev state machine

**Artifacts**

- `journal/2026-04-13-step-function-routing.md` — full decision log

body:
## Summary
- Étend F-IA-03 à **F-FA-05 Partage immobilier** sur 2 champs numériques (`valeurVenale` et `capitalRestantDu`).
- Source IA seule, seuil 10 %, **warning uniquement** (pattern factuel comme SF-IA-03-04 F-DT-07).
- Logique **"référence import > best-match"** : utilise la valeur importée via SF-FA-05-04 si disponible, sinon l'item le plus proche numériquement dans la liste filtrée.
- **Termine la couverture du domaine famille** (F-FA-05, F-FA-06, F-FA-07 tous couverts).

## Mini-spec
`docs/features/F-IA-03/SF-IA-03-08-coherence-partage-immobilier.md`

## Logique de référence

1. Si l'avocat a importé un bien via SF-FA-05-04 → référence = valeur importée exacte
2. Sinon → `findBestMatch(userValue, filteredList)` retourne l'item dont la valeur est numériquement la plus proche
3. Si l'écart relatif user/référence ≥ 10 % → `warning`

## Règles

| Condition | Comportement |
|---|---|
| User valeur = 0 ou vide | pas d'alerte |
| `liquidationCommunaute` null | pas d'alerte |
| Liste filtrée vide (aucun bien immo / aucun prêt) | pas d'alerte |
| Écart < 10 % | pas d'alerte |
| Résultat F-FA-05 sauvegardé | alertes gelées |

## Hors scope explicite

- Surveillance de `quotePartAttributaire` : non extraite par l'IA, presque toujours 50 % en pratique
- Surveillance de `country` / `isDivorce` : choix produit, pas factuels
- Sources F-96 / questions IA : non pertinentes pour champs purement numériques

## Changements
- `PartageImmobilierSectionComponent` :
  - Helper `findBestMatch(value, list)` pure
  - Types `PartageCoherenceAlert`, `PartageAlertField = 'VALEUR_VENALE' | 'CAPITAL_RESTANT'`
  - Signaux privés `importedValeurVenale`, `importedCapital` mis à jour par `applyImport()`
  - Computed `coherenceAlerts` (fallback best-match)
  - Computed `alertsSummary` (blockers toujours 0)
  - `alertTooltip` avec libellé + valeur formatée €
- Template : bandeau récap + badges à côté des champs (complémentaires aux provenance notes SF-FA-05-04)

## Tests
**857 frontend verts** (12 nouveaux + 13 de SF-FA-05-04 + 4 initiaux).

Matrice surveillée :
- Valeur dans les 10 % → pas d'alerte
- 10 %+ → warning
- Best-match préfère l'item le plus proche
- Import actif neutralise le best-match (référence = imported)
- User = 0 → silence
- `liquidationCommunaute` null → silence
- Aucun bien immobilier détecté → silence
- Capital : mêmes règles
- Compteur mixte (2 alertes, 0 blockers)
- Freeze quand résultat chargé

## Test plan
- [ ] Dossier FAMILLE FR : IA détecte "Maison principale 400 000 €". Saisir 410 000 € (+2.5%) → aucune alerte. Saisir 470 000 € (+17.5%) → badge orange warning, tooltip "L'IA a détecté : Maison principale — 400 000 €".
- [ ] Dossier avec 2 biens IA (Maison 400k, Appartement 300k) + user 310 000 → best match = Appartement, écart 3.3% → aucune alerte.
- [ ] Importer Maison via le panneau SF-FA-05-04 puis modifier à 350 000 € → warning vs Maison 400 000 € (pas de glissement vers Appartement 300k).
- [ ] Pareil pour capital restant dû avec prêts détectés.
- [ ] Dossier sans IA / liquidationCommunaute → comportement inchangé.
- [ ] Générer la simulation puis recharger → alertes gelées.

author: jmf-pobox
body:
## Summary

Two new docs capturing recent planning conversations around Postern's future.

## What changed

### `docs/ideas.md`
Captures a forward-looking pitch for repositioning Postern as a Pharo release engineering tool rather than just "the Claude SDK's image driver." Includes:

- Target-audience map (release engineer, package maintainer, release QA, VM developer, agent-driven dev)
- Endpoint ideas: `/info` (environment fingerprint), `/smoke` (scripted test battery), Pharo-version-aware `/help`
- `postern-matrix` CLI sketch for multi-image orchestration
- Distribution channels: Pharo Catalog, companion `pharo-ci-matrix` repo, ESUG talk
- Three principles to preserve: stay tiny and stable, zero Anthropic surface, path to Pharo core adoption

None of these are commitments — the file exists so the conversation has a durable artifact to return to.

### `docs/pharo-compat.md`
The configuration management plan for extending stable Postern to Pharo 13 and 14. Key decisions:

- **Single `main` branch**, shared `Postern-Core`, per-version `Postern-Compat-PharoN` shim packages selected via Metacello `for: #'pharoN.x'` conditionals
- Rejects long-lived version branches, parallel packages, and runtime `Smalltalk version` checks with rationale for each
- Six-PR execution plan: introduce compat seam on Pharo 12 first, rewrite baseline, add Pharo 13, add CI matrix, add Pharo 14, update docs/release
- BaselineOfPostern structure example
- Four signals that the structure is breaking down (compat package growth, cherry-picking, core-API divergence, stray version checks)

## Scope note

The first commit (`06f6351`) also incidentally carries `.beads/interactions.jsonl` and `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Those were sitting untracked in the worktree (not gitignored), so `git add docs/ideas.md` swept them in. The content is Punt Labs tracker state that predates this PR — legitimate content, off-topic for a docs-only PR. Merge as-is or ask me to amend, your call.

## Test plan

- [x] Markdown lint clean on both new files locally
- [x] No code or build changes

> Low functional risk since changes are documentation-only, but it introduces `.beads/issues.jsonl` tracker content that may be unintended/sensitive to ship publicly.

author: bencap
body:
The score set search query filtered out superseded score sets using a LEFT OUTER JOIN on the superseding_score_set relationship. Because replaces_id has no unique constraint, score sets with multiple superseding versions produced N rows per original, all counted against the SQL LIMIT. This caused paginated searches to return fewer unique score sets than requested (~84 instead of 100 on prod).

Replace the LEFT JOIN + OR filter with a NOT EXISTS subquery (via .has()), which produces exactly one row per score set regardless of how many superseders exist. Also strengthens the regression test to use multiple keywords per experiment and adds a new test for the multiple-superseders scenario.

Opens #706, which is the root cause of this issue. This fix mitigates consequences for the search endpoint specifically, but does not address all issues caused by the bug.

Although it turns out the `joined_loads` weren't the root cause of this specific issue, I'm leaving the new `select_in_loads` as they still represent an improvement over the prior code and could protect us from future row multiplication.

author: kvfxkaido
body:
## Summary

Closes out the daemon-wiring portion of **Phase 6** from `docs/decisions/push-runtime-v2.md`. Before this PR, `handleSubmitTaskGraph` threw "Coder delegation is not yet wired" on any coder node and there was no `delegate_coder` RPC at all — only explorer and reviewer had daemon-side homes. This PR mirrors the existing explorer scaffold pattern for the Coder role so task-graph coder nodes stop failing fast and `delegate_coder` becomes a real RPC.

### What ships

- **`runScaffoldCoderForTaskGraph`** helper in `cli/pushd.ts`. Invokes `runCoderAgent` from `lib/coder-agent.ts` with the same stubbed tool executor / detector / `evaluateAfterModel` pattern as the explorer scaffold, plus the four coder-specific option fields (`sandboxId: ''`, `sandboxToolProtocol: ''`, `verificationPolicyBlock: null`, `approvalModeBlock: null`) that fill the kernel's richer option surface. LLM streams real tokens via the daemon provider adapter; any tool call the model emits receives a canned "not yet wired" result; the run produces a `DelegationOutcome` marked `status: 'inconclusive'` with `missingRequirements` pointing at the stub.
- **`handleDelegateCoder`** RPC handler. Full copy of the `handleDelegateExplorer` lifecycle adapted to coder — resolves `configure_role_routing.coder`, emits real `subagent.*` events with `agent: 'coder'`, persists a `DelegationOutcome` record to session state, and claims terminal ownership synchronously before any awaited event emission so `cancel_delegation` races resolve deterministically (same contract as explorer). Coder-specific error code is `CODER_FAILED`.
- **Task-graph executor** in `handleSubmitTaskGraph` — `agent: 'coder'` now calls `runScaffoldCoderForTaskGraph` instead of throwing. Reordered the dispatch so explorer and coder land in their scaffold helpers symmetrically.
- **Registered `delegate_coder` in HANDLERS + advertised `delegation_coder_v1`.** `multi_agent` stays unadvertised — the real Coder tool executor is still the remaining gate.

### What's deliberately out of scope

- **Real daemon-side Coder tool executor** (filesystem ops, approval binding, acceptance-criteria runner) — the biggest remaining chunk of Phase 6 and too large for a single PR. Today the scaffold proves the kernel is reachable; real tool exec slots into the `stubToolExec` seam in a follow-up.
- **v1 synthetic downgrade** — independent from the coder work, small enough for its own follow-up PR.
- **Approval callback wiring** — blocked on the real Coder tool executor (there is no kernel-side tool to gate approvals on yet).

### Tests

author: copilot
body:
Node role users upgrading to Server+Desktop triggered an immediate `nixos-rebuild` before configuring domains, SSL email, or port forwarding — causing the build to fail because Caddy and newly-activated services (Synapse, Vaultwarden, Nextcloud, etc.) require that config.

## Changes

- **`api_upgrade_to_server()`** — replace rebuild with reboot; the role is written to `role-state.nix` and onboarding flag is cleared, then the system reboots straight into the wizard (which now shows steps 3 & 4 since role is `server_plus_desktop`)
- **`api_onboarding_complete()`** — trigger `sovran-hub-rebuild.service` here instead; by this point all domain/SSL/port config is persisted and the build succeeds
- **`doUpgradeToServer()` (events.js)** — after the upgrade API returns, show a rebooting message and poll `/api/ping`; redirect to `/onboarding` once the server is back

```
Before: write role-state.nix → rebuild (fails, no domains) → reboot → onboarding (too late)
After:  write role-state.nix → reboot → onboarding (collects domains/SSL/ports) → rebuild ✓
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

When a user in the **Node** role clicks "Upgrade to Server+Desktop", the system immediately triggers a `nixos-rebuild` via `sovran-hub-rebuild.service` **before** the user has had any chance to configure domains, SSL email, or port forwarding. This causes a build error because:

1. Switching to `server_plus_desktop` activates services like Matrix Synapse, Vaultwarden, Nextcloud, WordPress, etc. (via `role-logic.nix` — the node role sets `synapse`, `vaultwarden`, `wordpress`, `nextcloud` to `false`, but `server_plus_desktop` defaults them all to `true`)
2. Caddy's config generator (`caddy.nix`) needs domain files in `/var/lib/domains/` and an SSL email — which don't exist yet for node users since they never went through steps 3 and 4 of onboarding (those steps are skipped for node role per `ROLE_SKIP_STEPS` in `onboarding.js`)
3. The rebuild fails, the system reboots, and starts back in onboarding — but by then the build already failed

### Current broken flow

1. User clicks "Upgrade" in the Hub sidebar (Node role)
2. `doUpgradeToServer()` in `events.js` calls `POST /api/role/upgrade-to-server`
3. `api_upgrade_to_server()` in `server.py` (line ~1752):
   - Writes `role-state.nix` setting `server_plus_desktop = true`
   - Removes `ONBOARDING_FLAG` (so onboarding re-runs)
   - **Immediately starts `sovran-hub-rebuild.service`** ← THIS IS THE BUG
4. Rebuild fails because domains/ports/SSL email aren't configured
5. System reboots → lands in onboarding wizard → user configures domains → but the initial rebuild already failed

### Expected flow (after fix)

1. User clicks "Upgrade"
2. Backend writes `role-state.nix`, removes onboarding flag
3. **Backend reboots instead of rebuilding** — no rebuild yet
4. System boots → Hub detects onboarding incomplete → redirects to onboarding wizard
5. The role is now `server_plus_desktop` so steps 3 (domains) and 4 (ports) are NOT skipped
6. User configures all domains, SSL email, port forwarding through the wizard
7. User clicks "Finish Setup" on step 5
8. **`/api/onboarding/complete` triggers the rebuild** — now all config is in place
9. Rebuild succeeds ✓

## Required Changes

### 1. `app/sovran_systemsos_web/server.py` — `/api/role/upgrade-to-server` endpoint (line ~1749-1786)

Replace the rebuild logic with a reboot. The endpoint should:
- Still write `role-state.nix`
- Still remove `ONBOARDING_FLAG`
- **NOT start the rebuild unit**
- Instead, issue a `reboot` command (same as `REBOOT_COMMAND = ["reboot"]` already defined)
- Return `{"ok": True, "status": "rebooting_to_onboarding"}`

```python
@app.post("/api/role/upgrade-to-server")
async def api_upgrade_to_server():
    """Upgrade from Node role to Server+Desktop role."""
    cfg = load_config()
    if cfg.get("role", "server_plus_desktop") != "node":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Upgrade is only available for the Node role.")

    try:
        with open("/etc/nixos/role-state.nix", "w") as f:
            f.write(ROLE_STATE_NIX)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Failed to write role-state.nix: {exc}")

    # Reset onboarding so the wizard runs for the newly unlocked services
    try:
        os.remove(ONBOARDING_FLAG)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass

    # Don't rebuild yet — the user needs to configure domains, SSL email,
    # and ports first via the onboarding wizard. Reboot so onboarding runs.
    try:
        await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*REBOOT_COMMAND)
    except Exception:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Failed to initiate reboot")

    return {"ok": True, "status": "rebooting_to_onboarding"}
```

### 2. `app/sovran_systemsos_web/server.py` — `/api/onboarding/complete` endpoint (line ~1678-1686)

After marking onboarding complete, trigger a NixOS rebuild so the new role's services are activated with the freshly configured domains/ports:

```python
@app.post("/api/onboarding/complete")
async def api_onboarding_complete():
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(ONBOARDING_FLAG), exist_ok=True)
    try:
        with open(ONBOARDING_FLAG, "w") as f:
            f.write("")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Could not write flag file: {exc}")

    # Trigger a NixOS rebuild now that domains/ports/SSL are configured.
    # This is especially important after a role upgrade (Node → Server+Desktop)
    # where the rebuild was deferred until onboarding collected all required config.
    try:
        open(REBUILD_LOG, "w").close()
    except OSError:
        pass

    await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        "systemctl", "reset-failed", REBUILD_UNIT,
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        "systemctl", "start", "--no-block", REBUILD_UNIT,
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    await proc.wait()...

</details>

body:
Email (SMTP) #1 — email_service.py handles all outbound email. Branded HTML template with BOSS header. Ready-made senders for mentions, HR (interview invites, offer letters, rejections), daily digest, and system alerts. Works with Gmail, Office 365, Mailgun, Sendinblue. To activate: add SMTP credentials to .env (see smtp_config_patch.py for Gmail App Password instructions).
Scheduled Messages #8 — Click the clock icon in the chat header → type message → pick date/time → Schedule. A background worker checks every 30 seconds and delivers it through WebSocket exactly on time. View/cancel pending scheduled messages via the calendar icon.
Pinned Messages #9 — Click ⋯ on any message → Pin. Pinned messages appear in the 📌 panel in the chat header with a count badge. Broadcasting via WebSocket so all users see the pin notification instantly.
Message Edit #10 — Click ⋯ → Edit on your own messages. The message input fills with the current text, a blue "Editing" bar appears at the bottom, and sending submits the edit. Full edit history stored in message_edits table. Edited messages show "(edited)" label. Synced to all users via WebSocket.
Group Audio/Video Calls #11 — Click 📞 or 📹 in the chat header. Uses WebRTC peer-to-peer — no server needed for the actual audio/video, only the signaling goes through your WebSocket. Works between any browsers supporting WebRTC (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari).
Screen Sharing #12 — During a call, click the 🖥️ button. Uses getDisplayMedia() — the user picks a window, tab, or entire screen. Replaces the video track in all peer connections so remote participants see the screen. One click stops it and restores the camera feed.

body:
## What

- Step-tab clicks in the viewer no longer call `updateStepProgress`, so clicking "Plan" while the workflow is on `implement` stops rewriting `.spec-context.json` `currentStep` to `plan`
- In-viewer tab clicks now take the same full-HTML regeneration path as sidebar navigation, so both produce identical header badge, footer buttons, and tab appearance
- Currently viewed step gets a solid accent outline; dashed outline when reviewing a step that isn't the workflow phase
- `deriveHighlights` now filters out steps whose document doesn't exist, even when history says they're completed (R003)
- Tab ✓ icon is gated on actual file existence, not just history
- `computeBadgeText` and `deriveViewerState` accept optional `viewedStep` + `stepDocExists` (unit-tested; reserved for future UI that wants per-tab state)

## Why

Viewing a completed earlier step used to silently mutate the spec's persisted state and make the badge/highlights lie. Unifying on the sidebar's render path keeps the visual state truthful and consistent across entry points.

## Testing

- [ ] Open a spec where `currentStep: implement`; click Plan tab — `.spec-context.json` `currentStep` stays `implement`, badge stays "IMPLEMENTING…"
- [ ] Viewed tab shows an accent outline; tabs/footer match sidebar navigation
- [ ] `npm test` — 26 suites, 249 tests green

author: trecek
body:
## Summary `tests/execution/test_recording_sigterm.py` synchronizes with a child FastMCP subprocess by string-matching a stderr log line (`"lifespan_started"`) that is emitted at `src/autoskillit/server/_lifespan.py:63` — BEFORE the lifespan's `try:` block and before anyio's cancel scope is fully wired around the `yield`. SIGTERM sent immediately after the token arrives at a frame outside the `try/finally`, so `recorder.finalize()` never runs, `scenario.json` is absent, the test fails, and the CI red cascades into the #801 parallel-pipeline deadlock. Prior patches bumped the deadline 5s → 15s → 30s and added `time.sleep(2.0)` without closing the race. The weakness is broader than this one test: **any code path that uses log-line string matching as a subprocess synchronization primitive is structurally vulnerable**, and the SIGTERM handler itself is installed via raw `signal.signal()` at `cli/app.py:126` — which delivers SIGTERM as a `KeyboardInterrupt` into whatever Python frame is currently executing, bypassing anyio's cancel-scope machinery entirely. Part A delivers three architectural immunity rails: 1. **Post-yield file sentinel as the readiness primitive.** Replace stderr log polling with a filesystem sentinel written from inside the lifespan's `try:` block. File existence is atomic — there is no string-parse race and no wall-clock settle-sleep. 2. **Event-loop-routed SIGTERM via `anyio.open_signal_receiver` at the `anyio.run()` boundary in `cli/app.py`.** Move SIGTERM handling into an async wrapper (`_serve_with_signal_guard`) that calls `anyio.create_task_group()` + `tg.start()` to arm the receiver *before* `mcp.run_async()` begins. Signal delivery becomes a scheduled asyncio callback rather than a frame-interrupting `KeyboardInterrupt`. 3. **Structural AST guards that make the anti-pattern impossible to reintroduce.** Three tests that fail red if anyone (a) emits a readiness log before the `try:` block of the lifespan, (b) calls `signal.signal(SIGTERM, ...)` outside an approved site, or (c) hand-rolls an inline stderr-readline readiness poll in a test. ━━━━━━━━━━
tg.start() blocks until

━━━━━━━━━━

author: dhsohn
body:
## Motivation

I added several features to improve the usability and functionality of Chemvas. Specifically, I implemented support for workbook tabs, integrated an xTB panel for advanced calculations, and fixed various hover issues across the application.

*   **Workbook Tabs:** Added tabbed navigation to manage different sheets within a single document.
*   **xTB Panel:** Integrated a dedicated panel to handle xTB calculations, providing users with more powerful computational chemistry tools directly in the UI.
*   **Hover Fixes:** Fixed several visual bugs related to hover states and selection handling to improve the user experience.

## Changes

*   I updated `README.md` to document the new features, including 2D -> 3D `.xyz` export and the dedicated xTB panel.
*   In `app/core/document_state.py`, I modified the state extraction logic to correctly handle wrapped LiteDraw payloads, supporting both bare states and workbook structures.
*   I updated `app/core/rdkit_adapter.py` by adding a new dataclass, `Molecule3DAtom`, to better manage 3D coordinates derived from RDKit.
*   I added the entire `xTB` integration logic in `app/core/xtb_adapter.py`, which handles file operations and communication with external xTB executables.
*   In `app/ui/canvas_view.py` and `app/ui/main_window.py`, I implemented structural changes to support the new tabbed interface (`QTabWidget`) and updated drawing logic to accommodate these additions.
*   I created a new dedicated UI component, `app/ui/xtb_panel.py`, which manages the layout and interaction for the xTB calculation panel.
*   I refactored `app/ui/preview_3d.py` to improve its structure and ensure compatibility with updated core components.
*   I updated `tests/test_core_document_io.py` to include tests covering document state serialization when using workbook structures.

## Verification

- I have tested the basic functionality of adding, switching, and managing multiple workbook tabs within a test document structure.
- I verified that the xTB panel correctly initializes and can execute placeholder calculations without crashing the main application loop.
- I confirmed that the 2D to 3D export feature works as expected for simple molecules.

body:
### 🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
### 💡 Vulnerability: Path Traversal
`file.originalname` input is unsanitized when constructing upload file paths for S3 keys or Local File Fallbacks. Attackers could potentially submit paths like `../../../etc/passwd` leading to S3 object structure pollution and, worse, arbitrary file system writes during local fallback usage. `subfolder` input is also not validated against directory traversal sequences in `files.service.ts`.
### 🎯 Impact
Could allow attackers to write arbitrary files locally in worst cases and severely pollute S3 keys.
### 🔧 Fix
- Used `path.basename(file.originalname)` across all original file name usages in `files.service.ts` and `site-capture.service.ts`.
- Validated `subfolder` using strict regex in `files.service.ts`.
- Replaced inline `require('path')` and `require('fs')` with module-level imports.

### ✅ Verification
- Build and tested via npm commands ensuring previous test coverage matches.
- Handled code review feedbacks and addressed missing places where `path.basename` was neglected.

author: srosro
body:
## Summary

Builds on #11 (@wesm's agentsview collector). Ships tkmx-client **v1.3.0** with agentsview as a hard dependency for all local Claude + Codex token collection, including `EXTRA_CLAUDE_CONFIGS`. Deletes `ccusage` support entirely. Users who prefer the old flow can `git checkout v1.2.0` — that tag is pushed and represents the last ccusage-based release.

Also folds in a correctness fix for `reporter/outcomes.js` (pre-existing bug, caught in review) that filters git stats to the user's own commits.

## Why not v2.0.0?

v1.2.0 has only been in the wild for 3 days and is currently the **most-deployed version** (12 users, 20 machines). Jumping straight to v2.0.0 three days later signals more churn than this change warrants. This is technically a SemVer violation — the agentsview hard dep *is* a breaking change — but for a pre-launch tool with a small user base we picked the minor-bump social contract over strict SemVer:

- The hard-fail error message is actionable (install one-liner + explicit v1.2.0 pin escape hatch)
- 12 users is small enough to handle directly if anyone gets stuck
- Early-stage tools (Rails for years) bump minor for breaking changes all the time
- Burning \"v2.0\" on what is essentially an internal collector swap would box us in for future user-facing pivots

README Upgrading section calls this out loudly so nobody's surprised.

## What you get by upgrading

1. **Correct codex token counts.** agentsview picks up cache-read tokens that the v1.x `~/.codex/state_*.sqlite` reader was silently dropping. Concretely: codex `total_tokens` jumps ~+92% for active codex users. This is a **correction, not inflation** — the tokens were always being spent, they just weren't being counted. Framed as \"now counted correctly\" on the leaderboard, not \"Sam is cheating.\"
2. **Accurate cost.** agentsview computes per-field costs via LiteLLM and the server respects client-provided cost (`tkmx-server/server/db.js:414`). The blended fallback the server used to apply goes away for codex — no more $X over/under-estimate.
3. **Speed.** ~200× faster than walking JSONL transcripts on large histories. Incremental sync means re-runs are cheap.
4. **Free session viewer as a side benefit.** You now have `agentsview` installed — run `agentsview` in a terminal and you get a full local web UI for browsing/searching every Claude + Codex session you've ever had, with full-text search. It's a real product, not a data-access tool. (See https://agentsview.io)
5. **Single install story going forward.** One dependency to install, not \"ccusage or agentsview or the codex sqlite reader depending on which flag you set.\"

Real-usage numbers from my three machines (v1.2.0 → v1.3.0):

| Machine | v1.2.0 total | v1.3.0 total | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mac (heavy codex+claude) | 3.85B | 4.46B | +610M (+15.9%) |
| linux #1 (mid codex) | 986M | 1.09B | +101M (+10.3%) |
| linux #2 (no codex) | 21.75M | 21.76M | ~0% |

The deltas are codex cache-read tokens that v1.x was missing. Machines without codex usage see no change.

## Breaking changes

- **agentsview is required**. Missing on PATH = fatal startup error with an actionable install message (includes the one-liner, `AGENTSVIEW_BIN` override hint, and v1.2.0 pin escape hatch).
- `USE_AGENTSVIEW` and `CCUSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` env vars removed. Ignored if present in `.env`.
- `reporter/claude-collect.js` deleted (ccusage wrapper).
- `collectCodexUsage` removed from `reporter/codex.js` (daily codex collection now via agentsview; the per-session stats helpers used under `REPORT_DEV_STATS=true` are preserved).
- Test counts: **65 → 68** on this branch. 9 tests in `test/claude-collect.test.js` and 7 tests in the `collectCodexUsage` suite in `test/codex.test.js` were deleted alongside the code they covered. 11 new tests added in `test/agentsview.test.js` (parser + resolver + AGENTSVIEW_BIN override + PATH fallback + executability check), 3 new tests in `test/outcomes.test.js` covering the author-filter fix, and 4 modified resolver tests.

## Escape hatch

Users who can't or don't want to install agentsview can pin to the last ccusage-based release:

```bash
cd tkmx-client
git checkout v1.2.0
npm install
npm run report
```

The `v1.2.0` tag is pushed to origin (verified: `54ce584b9de342087fdcfdd753d00be52ec87877`).

## EXTRA_CLAUDE_CONFIGS routing

Agentsview already supports alternate Claude homes via `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR` + `AGENT_VIEWER_DATA_DIR` (verified at `internal/parser/types.go:66`, `internal/config/config.go:466`, `internal/sync/engine.go:1051`, `scripts/e2e-server.sh:43-45`). For each `EXTRA_CLAUDE_CONFIGS` entry we:

1. Append `/projects` to the entry to match agentsview's expected path
2. Compute a stable per-entry `AGENT_VIEWER_DATA_DIR` at `~/.agentsview-tkmx/<sha256[:16] of abs path>/` so incremental sync stays partitioned per remote mirror
3. Invoke `collectAgentsviewClaudeOnly(bin, since, env)` with both env vars set
4. Catch per-iteration failures so one bad remote dir doesn't crash the whole report run (matches the v1.x ccusage behavior)

## Sync scoping (verified)

One call to `agentsview usage daily --agent claude` (without `--no-sync`) syncs **every** agent, not just claude. Verified at `agentsview/internal/sync/engine.go:1034 syncAllLocked`, which iterates `parser.Registry` in a single pass and discovers files for all agent types. The follow-up `--agent codex --no-sync` query is therefore safe; codex data is already fresh from the first call. Comment added in `reporter/agentsview.js` documenting this coupling so a future agentsview change to per-agent sync scoping will surface as a visible assumption to fix.

## Also in this PR: outcomes.js author filter

Caught during review of this branch: `collectOutcomeStats` (added in 6752a1a) was running `git log` with no `--author` filter, so `commits` / `loc_added` / `loc_removed` / `files_changed` summed across every author in every repo Claude Code touched — including shared-team codebases and read-only clones. PR stats were already correct via `gh pr list --author=@me`; only the git-log side was broken.

Fixed across four commits:
1. Read each repo's configured `user.email` via `git config` and pass it as `--author=...` to `git log`.
2. Track `authoredRepos` by repos where the filter returned at least one commit in the window, so `repos_active` reflects actual contributions (a freshly-cloned read-only repo no longer counts as \"active\").
3. Force `--local` scope with a `--global` fallback so commits don't disappear when the user changes their global `user.email` — the author lookup now matches how commits were actually authored at the time, not just the current global identity.
4. Anchor `--author=<email>` with literal angle brackets so the email isn't interpreted as a POSIX ERE substring match — `sam@acme.com` no longer accidentally matches `notsam@acme.com`, and `+` / `.` metachars in email addresses don't silently change semantics.

**Real-repo impact** (so's profile, 28-day window):
- commits: 1,446 → **825** (−43%)
- loc_added: 861,202 → **447,435** (−48%)
- loc_removed: 153,244 → **76,262** (−50%)
- repos_active: 12 → **11** (agentsview dropped — inspected only, zero commits)

This is a correction, not a regression. Pre-launch is the window for it.

## Agentsview resolver hardening

- `AGENTSVIEW_BIN` env override added for nix / asdf / custom install locations
- Fallback to `\$PATH` via `env which agentsview` when no hard-coded candidate exists
- Candidates now verified as **executable files** (`X_OK` + `isFile`), so a stale directory named `agentsview` or a non-executable drop can't resolve and then crash opaquely during invocation
- `queryAgent` wraps `execFileSync` errors as `agentsview <agent> query failed: <stderr>` so the top-level `Fatal:` line is actionable
- stderr of expected-failure git/gh probes in `outcomes.js` now routed to /dev/null, so reporter output and log files stay clean instead of leaking \"fatal: not a git repository\" on every run

author: jurywang
body:
## Summary This PR refactors the AI analysis generation system to request plain text output from the LLM instead of HTML, then parse it into structured HTML cards on the client side. This improves robustness by eliminating the risk of LLM-generated HTML/CSS breaking the page layout. ## Key Changes - **Simplified LLM prompt**: Changed system prompt to explicitly forbid HTML, Markdown, and code syntax. The model now outputs only plain text with section headers marked by `===Title===` delimiters. - **New `parseAiResponse()` function**: Implements client-side parsing that: - Strips any remaining Markdown/code artifacts from the raw text - Splits content by section headers (`===Title===`) - Maps section titles to predefined card classes and icons - Converts paragraphs into proper HTML structure with `

` tags - Provides fallback rendering if the model doesn't follow the expected format - **Updated data formatting**: Changed from sending raw JSON to the LLM to sending a human-readable text summary of app metrics, making it easier for the model to process and reducing token usage. - **CSS refinement**: Replaced aggressive `all: unset` rule in `.ai-analysis-content *` with selective property inheritance (`font-family`, `color`, `line-height`) to prevent unintended style breakage while still isolating the content. ## Implementation Details - The parser handles five predefined sections: 整体大盘分析, 头部应用亮点, 问题应用诊断, 运营建议, and 趋势洞察 - Each section is rendered as a separate card with an emoji icon and title - Paragraphs are separated by blank lines in the plain text and converted to individual `

` elements - If parsing fails (model doesn't follow format), content is rendered as a single fallback card - All HTML/script/style tag injection attempts are stripped during parsing https://claude.ai/code/session_01Q2qxk1tKqorJiz1R1SwLRV

author: clintmod
body:
## Summary

`Vars.ToCacheMap` held `vars.mutex.RLock()` and then called `vars.Len()`, which re-acquires the same `sync.RWMutex`. Go's `RWMutex` is **not reentrant** — from the stdlib docs, a pending `Lock` excludes new readers from acquiring the lock. So in the common no-writer case this works, but if a writer queues between the outer `RLock()` and the inner `Len()`'s `RLock()`, the inner call blocks forever. Classic latent deadlock.

Replace the inner `vars.Len()` call with `vars.om.Len()` directly. The outer `RLock` already protects `om`, so there's no second acquisition. One-line fix with a short comment explaining why.

Fixes #6

author: clintmod
body:
## Summary

`taskfile.RemoteExists` uses `defer resp.Body.Close()` inside the `for _, taskfile := range DefaultTaskfiles` retry loop. `defer` fires at function return, not loop-iteration end — so every non-OK retry stacked another deferred close against the current `resp`, and because `resp` is reassigned on the next iteration, each prior response body's FD was leaked until the enclosing function returned.

Fix: record `resp.StatusCode` then close the body inline at the end of each iteration, so each retry releases its FD before the next request and a successful match still returns with a closed body. Single file touched.

Fixes #5

author: dawoudio
body:
## Summary

The repo referenced `cypress.config.ts` (root) and `docker/cypress.config.ts` in **seven files** across dev docs, skill docs, and real runtime code, but **neither file exists in this repo**. The actual Cypress config files live under `cypress/configs/` and every `npm run test*` script passes them via `--config-file`:

```
package.json:
"test":            "npx cypress run --config-file cypress/configs/docker.config.ts",
"test:open":       "npx cypress open --e2e --config-file cypress/configs/docker.config.ts ...",
"test:api":        "npx cypress run --config-file cypress/configs/docker.config.ts --spec ...",
"test:ui":         "npx cypress run --config-file cypress/configs/docker.config.ts --spec ...",
"test:new-system": "npx cypress run --config-file cypress/configs/new-system.config.ts"
```

There is **no** root `cypress.config.ts` in this repo and Cypress is never asked to auto-detect one.

## ⚠️ Rebased onto master after #8655 merged

This branch was originally based on master before #8655 landed. After #8655 merged with the (also bad) boxed warning in cypress-testing.md, this branch rebased cleanly onto current master. The merge conflict in the `Configuration Location` section L97-132 (where both branches touched the same lines) was resolved by **keeping the `cypress/configs/*` version**, and the boxed warning that landed via #8655 was also rewritten in this commit so it points at the correct files.

The L774 NOTE wording was improved by an in-branch commit (`6ed0b21 Update cypress-testing.md`, co-authored by Copilot via @DawoudIO's review). That improvement is preserved in this rebase — Cypress *will* run without `--config-file`, but it falls back to defaults that don't carry ChurchCRM's `env` / `baseUrl` / `specPattern`.

## The most damaging version of this bug

`cypress/support/ui-commands.js` throws three runtime errors when credentials are missing:

```js
throw new Error('Admin credentials not configured in cypress.config.ts env: ...');
throw new Error('Standard user credentials not configured in cypress.config.ts env: ...');
throw new Error('No-finance user credentials not configured in cypress.config.ts env: ...');
```

**Contributors hitting these errors would grep for a file that was never there.** Fixing these error messages is the biggest single contributor-experience win in this PR.

## Files fixed (7)

| # | File | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `cypress/support/ui-commands.js` | 3 thrown error messages in `setupAdminSession` / `setupStandardSession` / `setupNoFinanceSession` + 3 corresponding JSDoc blocks now point at `cypress/configs/docker.config.ts` |
| 2 | `cypress/support/e2e.js` | Comment about `installLogsPrinter` location corrected to `cypress/configs/_shared.ts` (`setupCommonNodeEvents`) — verified that's where it's actually registered |
| 3 | `.agents/skills/churchcrm/cypress-testing.md` | 5 locations: `Configuration Location` rewritten, the boxed warning that landed via #8655 also rewritten, `Cypress Config Files` NOTE flipped (with @DawoudIO's improved Copilot-co-authored wording preserved), 2 code-example comments (`cy.task()` registration + cross-spec env example) updated |
| 4 | `.agents/skills/churchcrm/testing.md` | 3 locations: Test Structure list, Credentials Configuration section, Files summary |
| 5 | `.agents/skills/churchcrm/development-workflows.md` | Cypress files list updated to the real `cypress/configs/` set |
| 6 | `cypress/README.md` | Stale migration TODO ("remove `cypress.json` in favor of `cypress.config.ts`") replaced with a factual note that configs already live under `cypress/configs/` and scripts pass `--config-file` |
| 7 | `tsconfig.json` | Drop `exclude` entries for the non-existent `cypress.config.ts` and `docker/cypress.config.ts`. The existing `cypress/configs/*` exclude is the only one that was ever doing anything. |

## Verification

- `grep -rn 'cypress\.config\.ts\|docker/cypress\.config' .agents/skills/churchcrm/ cypress/support/ cypress/README.md tsconfig.json` → only **negative** mentions remain (e.g. "there is no root `cypress.config.ts`"); no stale positive references

An unrestricted, default CORS configuration allows any origin to make cross-origin requests. In an API Gateway, this exposes the service to potential unauthorized use from malicious origins unless properly controlled.

author: clintmod
body:
## Summary

`rite migrate` only rewrote the *first* `.TASK` / `.TASK_DIR` reference when two shared a separator inside a single `{{ … }}` expression. `{{.TASK .TASK}}` became `{{.RITE_NAME .TASK}}`; `{{printf \"%s/%s\" .TASK_DIR .TASK_DIR}}` left the second `.TASK_DIR` un-rewritten.

## Root cause

The boundary regexes in `internal/task/migrate.go`:

```go
rxTaskDirRef  = regexp.MustCompile(`(^|[^.\w])\.TASK_DIR([^\w]|$)`)
rxTaskNameRef = regexp.MustCompile(`(^|[^.\w])\.TASK([^_\w]|$)`)
```

simulate word boundaries via bracket classes because Go's RE2 has no lookahead. The bracket classes *consume* the separator characters on both sides of each match. When two refs share a separator (the space in `{{.TASK .TASK}}`), `ReplaceAllString` advances past the region match #1 consumed — so the shared separator is no longer available as the lead boundary for match #2.

## Fix

Run each replacement to a fixed point inside `rewriteSpecialVarRefs`. The `${1}…${2}` replacement preserves both boundary chars in the output, so re-scanning the result string finds the next match. Cost is O(n) passes per expression in the pathological case; in practice 1–2.

Not a runtime correctness bug — both `.TASK`/`.TASK_DIR` and `.RITE_NAME`/`.RITE_TASK_DIR` resolve via `compiler.getSpecialVars`. But the migrate tool's job is to leave converted Ritefiles on the SPEC-preferred surface, and a half-migrated diff misleads users auditing the rewrite.

## Tests

New table-driven `TestMigrateRewritesAdjacentSpecialVars` in `internal/task/migrate_test.go` with six cases:

- two `.TASK_DIR` space-separated
- two `.TASK_DIR` inside `printf`
- two `.TASK` space-separated
- three `.TASK_DIR` space-separated
- mixed `.TASK` + `.TASK_DIR` in one expression
- separate-expression control case (`{{.TASK}}{{.TASK_DIR}}`)

Verified test fails on `main` and passes with the fix applied.

Fixes #10

- [x] `go test ./internal/task/` → ok
- [x] new test fails before fix, passes after

author: odow
body:
I am migrating the InfrastructureModels ecosystem away from Memento.jl.

See https://github.com/lanl-ansi/InfrastructureModels.jl/pull/99

PMD made this change a number of years ago. Your current design has a number of unforeseen consequences.

There are two main issues. The first is that this function mutates global state. If someone changes the logger after PMD, this function will erase their changes back to the global state _before_ PMD.

https://github.com/lanl-ansi/PowerModelsDistribution.jl/blob/79874bc491e9b2e71adb09bea79f227f33a99a72/src/core/logging.jl#L53-L54

The other issue (or feature, depending on how you see it) is that _every_ log must go through the PMD logger, even if they're completely unrelated.

https://github.com/lanl-ansi/PowerModelsDistribution.jl/blob/79874bc491e9b2e71adb09bea79f227f33a99a72/src/core/logging.jl#L78-L82

These aren't the end of the world (it's only logging), so merging this PR isn't strictly necessary. I mainly made this PR as an exercise to check that our logging strategy also works for PMD.

## test_log

There's one issue with my design: `@test_logs` works by replacing the global logger with something that caches the logs so it can parse them for the messages. Since we have a package-specific logger we need our own version of `_test_logs`.

body: ## Summary HyroTrader infrastructure improvements. The v4 playbook rewrite has been **reverted** after both Cursor and Claude independently confirmed it fails every prop challenge simulation variant. ### What's IN This PR (merge-ready) 1. **Compound edge filter** (`hyro_filter_from_dashboard.py:232-253`) - `trust_score >= 3 AND score >= 50 AND direction = LONG` - Lifts crypto PF from 1.57 → **3.09** (58.6% WR, CI lower bound 53%) - SHORT gate: requires `trust >= 5 AND score >= 60` - Independently verified by Cursor + Claude 2. **Expanded symbol universe** (`hyrotrader_short_term_scanner.py`) - 5 → 26 symbols in data-driven tiers - Tier 1 (PF > 2.0): BTC, ETH, XRP, SEI, FET, ETC - Tier 2 (PF 1.3-2.0): AVAX, APT, SOL, LINK, JUP, BNB, DOT - Removed: MATICUSDT (delisted, 738 ghost picks) 3. **Expanded daily workflow** (`hyro-daily.yml`) - Backtest symbols: 4 → 9 4. **Scanner threshold tuning** — relaxed to avoid filtering picks that pass the compound gate ### What's NOT in This PR (reverted) The v4 playbook rewrite (`hyro_live_strategies.json`) was reverted to the original after definitive failure: | Simulation | Result | Fail Reason | Total PnL | |---|---|---|---| | Concurrent (Cursor) | **FAIL** | Overall DD $509 > $500 | -$509 | | Concurrent (Claude) | **FAIL** | Daily DD $262 > $250 | +$186 | | Sequential 3d (Claude) | **FAIL** | Trailing DD $516 | -$302 | | Sequential 7d (Claude) | **FAIL** | Trailing DD $531 | -$358 | | Sequential 14d (Claude) | **FAIL** | Trailing DD $517 | -$414 | | Sequential 21d (Claude) | **FAIL** | Trailing DD $530 | -$384 | | Sequential 30d (Claude) | **FAIL** | Trailing DD $509 | -$149 | Root cause: the "proven" strategies are net-negative over 6 months under prop DD constraints. Not a correlation problem (sequential fails too), not a concurrency problem — structural edge problem. ### Failing Sim Artifacts (committed for transparency) - `audit_dashboard/data/hyro_playbook_combined.json` — Cursor's concurrent sim (FAIL) - Claude's artifacts on main: `hyro_portfolio_sim.json`, `hyro_portfolio_sim_risk05.json`, sequential sweep results ### Verification - `py_compile` on all Python files ✅ - Compound filter tested: 82 → 28 picks with gate active ✅ - SHORT gate confirmed at line 249-253 ✅

body: ## Purpose This PR is intended to adjust HunyuanImage3's default behavior that always generated the negative/unconditional branch, so generation can run in single-branch mode when guidance is not enabled. ## What This PR Changes 1. **Guidance behavior** - Allows `guidance_scale <= 1.0` without forcing it to `1.0 + epsilon`. - This enables true non-CFG behavior for low-guidance requests. 2. **CFG factor control** - Changes `cfg_factor` for `gen_image` from a fixed value to dynamic gating - CFG duplication is now enabled only when guidance is actually greater than 1. 3. **Tensor layout robustness** - Replaces `view(...)` with `reshape(...)` in the HunyuanImage3 attention output path to avoid runtime errors when tensors are non-contiguous. ## Test Plan Tested on 4x Ascend NPU with v0.18.0.post1 vllm omni Online ``` vllm serve "/data/HunyuanImage-3.0/" --omni --port "8091" \ --tensor_parallel_size 4 \ --log-stats \ --stage-configs-path "vllm_omni/platforms/npu/stage_configs/hunyuan_image3_moe_dit.yaml" ``` client ``` curl -X POST http://localhost:8091/v1/images/generations \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "prompt": "A cinematic medium shot captures a single Asian woman seated on a chair within a dimly lit room, creating an intimate and theatrical atmosphere. ### Motivation
- Evitar fallos al insertar usuarios cuando el `body` contiene campos no existentes en la tabla `User` (por ejemplo `role`) que rompían el `INSERT`.
- Aceptar payloads más flexibles desde el frontend permitiendo `role_id` o `role` (nombre o id numérico).
- Mejorar la retroalimentación al cliente devolviendo `400` cuando no hay campos válidos para crear el usuario.

### Description
- Añadido `USER_WRITABLE_COLUMNS` y la función `sanitizeUserPayload` en `src/models/users.models.js` para filtrar solo las columnas permitidas antes del `INSERT` y hashear la `password` allí mismo.
- Añadida la normalización de rol con `normalizeRoleId` y la búsqueda por nombre `getRoleByName` para resolver `role` (nombre o número) a `role_id` utilisando múltiples nombres de tabla candidatas.
- `createUser` en `src/models/users.models.js` ahora usa el payload saneado y lanza un error claro cuando no hay campos válidos para crear el usuario.
- Controlador `createUser` en `src/controllers/users.controllers.js` captura ese error y devuelve `400` con el mensaje apropiado en lugar de `500`.
- Esquema de validación actualizado en `src/schemas/users.schema.js` para aceptar `role_id` y `role` en formatos comunes y mantener `passthrough` para tolerancia.

### Testing

- Ejecutado `node --check src/schemas/users.schema.js` y la comprobación pasó correctamente.

body:
Closes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/2747

## Purpose

`/v1/audio/speech` crashes with `RuntimeError: Missing prefill_consumed_text_tokens` when called on Qwen3-Omni with async_chunk.

The generic fallback in `_prepare_speech_generation()` sent raw text without a chat template, causing `compute_talker_prompt_ids_length()` to return 0. This produced a 1-token placeholder that made the talker enter the decode path without a prior prefill.

This PR adds a guard: when the engine advertises a `"talker"` stage (Qwen3-Omni, Qwen2.5-Omni), raise a clear `ValueError` directing users to `/v1/chat/completions` with `"modalities": ["audio"]`. Other multi-stage audio backends (Dynin-Omni, MiMo-Audio) and generic single-stage backends are unaffected.

## Test Plan

Added `test_prepare_speech_rejects_non_tts_omni_model` in `tests/entrypoints/openai_api/test_serving_speech.py` which simulates the Qwen3-Omni stage layout (thinker/talker/code2wav) and asserts the `ValueError` is raised.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai_api/test_serving_speech.py::TestTTSMethods::test_prepare_speech_rejects_non_tts_omni_model -v
```

Existing tests (`test_create_speech_success`, `test_streaming`, `test_batch_success`) are unaffected since their fixtures have no `"talker"` stage.

## Test Result

- New test verifies the `ValueError` is raised for Qwen omni stage layouts.
- Existing speech endpoint tests remain green (guard only triggers on `"talker"` stage, not on generic/empty stage configs).

## Summary

SPEC §Scoping has zero direct coverage today. This adds four fixture-backed tests wired through the existing executor golden-fixture harness in `internal/task/scope_isolation_test.go`.

## Fixtures (all PASS against current code)

- **`parent_child`** — child task sets `vars: { V: child }`; parent calls child then echoes `{{.V}}`. Verifies child's task-scope var does not leak upward. ✅
- **`siblings`** — tasks A and B each declare `vars:`; B cannot reference A's task-scope `SECRET_A` (checked via both `{{.VAR}}` and shell-native `${VAR:-absent}`). ✅
- **`cross_include`** — entrypoint `includes: { a, b }`; A's `FROM_A` and B's `FROM_B` are mutually invisible. ✅
- **`nested_includes`** — A → B → C chain. C (grandchild) sees TOP (A) and MID (B); B does not see BOTTOM (C); A sees neither MID nor BOTTOM. Confirms vars flow downward only. ✅

## Adjacent finding (not in fixtures, orthogonal to scoping)

While authoring `nested_includes`, shell-native `${BOTTOM:-absent}` inside `c.yml` resolved to `absent` even though `c.yml` itself declares `vars: { BOTTOM: gamma }`. At entrypoint and 1-deep include tiers the equivalent works. This looks like a `vars:` export/unification issue at the 2-deep include tier, not a §Scoping bug — left out of the fixtures to keep the test focused. Worth a separate issue.

Closes #2
