author: thomasjiangcy
body:
## What was changed
This PR replaces shell-script-shaped runtime artifact installs with typed artifact operations that are compiled in TypeScript, carried through the sandbox runtime contract, and executed directly by `sandboxd`. It keeps a narrow first-class op set (`exec`, `mise_install`, `github_release_install`), migrates the existing Codex/Slack/Jira artifact definitions onto that model, removes the temporary compatibility path, and updates the generated contract/client surfaces plus integration coverage so sandbox profile compilation and sandbox startup both validate the new representation end to end.

Original symptom this addresses:
```text
Failed to initialize sandbox runtime.
E2B operation `init` failed: ... runtime plan artifacts[2] lifecycle.install[0] failed (artifactKey=slack-cli): command failed with exit code 22 (output=curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 403)
```

- `packages/integrations-core/src/types/index.ts`, `packages/integrations-core/src/runtime-plan/schema.ts`, `packages/integrations-core/src/runtime-plan/index.ts`, and `packages/integrations-core/src/validation/index.ts` now define, parse, and validate typed artifact install steps instead of raw command arrays.
- `packages/integrations-core/src/compiler/index.ts` lowers artifact helpers into typed steps, and the old shell-oriented GitHub helper wrappers were removed once all callers migrated.
- `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.ts`, `packages/integrations-definitions/src/slack/variants/slack-default/compile-binding.ts`, and `packages/integrations-definitions/src/jira/variants/jira-default/compile-binding.ts` now emit canonical typed artifact operations.
- `packages/sandboxd/src/runtime/plan.rs` and `packages/sandboxd/src/runtime/artifact_install.rs` now deserialize and execute typed artifact operations directly, including bounded retry logic for GitHub release downloads and typed validation errors for malformed plans.
- `packages/sandbox-runtime-contract/schemas/sandboxd-startup-input.schema.json` and the generated OpenAPI/client outputs under `apps/control-plane-api`, `apps/data-plane-api`, `apps/dashboard`, and `packages/data-plane-internal-client` were regenerated so the API surfaces match the new runtime plan shape.
- `packages/sandboxd/tests/runtime_plan_apply.rs`, `packages/integrations-core/src/compiler/index.test.ts`, `packages/integrations-core/integration/github-release-script.integration.test.ts`, and `apps/control-plane-api/integration/sandbox-profiles-compile-runtime-plan.integration.test.ts` were updated to assert the typed artifact-op flow end to end.

## How to review
- Start with `packages/integrations-core/src/types/index.ts` and `packages/integrations-core/src/runtime-plan/schema.ts` to see the final runtime artifact IR and its validation rules.
- Then read `packages/sandboxd/src/runtime/plan.rs` and `packages/sandboxd/src/runtime/artifact_install.rs` to review how those typed steps are decoded and executed inside `sandboxd`.
- After that, review `packages/integrations-core/src/compiler/index.ts` together with the migrated definitions in `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.ts`, `packages/integrations-definitions/src/slack/variants/slack-default/compile-binding.ts`, and `packages/integrations-definitions/src/jira/variants/jira-default/compile-binding.ts` to confirm the compiler emits the intended ops.
- Finish with `apps/control-plane-api/integration/sandbox-profiles-compile-runtime-plan.integration.test.ts` and `packages/sandboxd/tests/runtime_plan_apply.rs`; they give the clearest end-to-end evidence that compiled plans and sandbox execution now agree on the typed contract.
- If you want to review commit-by-commit, the consolidated branch still preserves the original stacked progression from compatibility scaffolding through sandboxd execution, helper migration, definition migration, and final compatibility removal.

## What the implication was
This moves artifact installation from opaque shell payloads to a shared typed contract between the compiler and `sandboxd`. That makes runtime-plan failures more classifiable, lets `sandboxd` apply operation-specific behavior like GitHub download retries, and gives us a cleaner base for future diagnostics or executor changes without pushing more ad hoc shell into integration definitions.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Integration definitions] --> B[integrations-core compiler]
  B --> C[Typed runtime artifact steps in startup input]
  C --> D[sandboxd plan parser]
  D --> E[Typed artifact executors]
  E --> F[Installed runtime tools inside sandbox]
```

## Checks and tests performed
- `pnpm format` validated that the consolidated branch tip is formatted correctly; the expected outcome was no formatter errors; it ran `oxfmt` across the repository and completed successfully.
- `pnpm lint` validated TS, OpenAPI, docs, SQL, and Rust linting against the rebased branch tip; the expected outcome was zero lint failures and no generated-spec drift; it ran the repository lint pipeline and completed successfully.
- `pnpm typecheck` validated the full workspace and script type surfaces; the expected outcome was that the typed artifact-op changes compile cleanly across apps, packages, and scripts; it ran the repo typecheck pipeline and completed successfully.
- `pnpm test` validated the workspace test suites against the consolidated branch; the expected outcome was that the typed runtime-plan changes preserve existing behavior while updating artifact-install assertions; it ran the repo test pipeline and completed successfully.
- `pnpm run ci` validated the same branch through the repository's full CI-equivalent TS and Rust flows; the expected outcome was a green end-to-end local CI pass including dashboard build, Storybook build, and `sandboxd` lint/typecheck/test; it ran successfully.

body:
This pull request introduces deterministic, seed-based key generation entry points to the FFI for both 32-bit and 64-bit BFV schemes, primarily to support reproducible integration testing. The main addition is a SHA-256-based deterministic random number generator, which enables generating the same secret key from the same seed, avoiding the need to store large binary fixtures. These seeded keygen functions are not intended for production use.

Deterministic key generation for integration testing:

* Added a SHA-256-counter-based deterministic pseudo-random number generator (`SeededRng`) that implements the `PseudoRandomNumberGenerator` protocol, enabling reproducible random streams from a fixed seed.
* Introduced a shared `seededKeygen` function that generates a secret key for any supported BFV scheme using the deterministic RNG, bypassing the default system RNG.
* Added new FFI entry points: `pnns64_keygen_seeded` and `pnns32_keygen_seeded`, which accept a seed and generate deterministic secret keys for 64-bit and 32-bit BFV, respectively, for integration test reproducibility. author: clintmod
body:
## Summary

Three new testdata fixtures + one test file (`internal/task/spec_behaviors_test.go`) covering SPEC behaviors that lacked direct end-to-end coverage.

| Fixture | What it asserts | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `testdata/precedence_shell_vs_cli/` | SPEC §Variable Precedence worked example — `VAR=shell rite task VAR=cli` with entrypoint and task-scope defaults resolves to `shell` in both `{{.VAR}}` and `$VAR`. Tier 1 beats 2/4/7. | PASS |
| `testdata/export_false/` | `export: false` — the var is visible to Go-template rendering but absent from the shell environ. | PASS |
| `testdata/lazy_dynamic/` | Task-scope `sh:` on an uninvoked task never fires. Verified via a sentinel file at `$LAZY_SENTINEL_PATH`. | PASS |

No SPEC violations surfaced.

## Gotcha — `$$SECRET` vs `$SECRET`

An `export: false` test can silently pass while the feature is broken. My first cut used `echo "env=$SECRET"` in `cmds:`, but rite's `${VAR}` preprocessor expands `$NAME` / `${NAME}` at template time from **all** vars regardless of the export flag — so the shell never looked `SECRET` up in its environ, and the test would have reported PASS even if `export: false` were a no-op.

The fixture now uses `$$SECRET`, which the preprocessor collapses to a literal `$SECRET` that reaches the shell. The shell then resolves against the real process environ — which is what the SPEC §Non-exported variables contract is actually about. An in-file comment documents this so the next person doesn't regress it.

Closes #3

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` clean (all three new tests PASS; no regressions)
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./internal/task/...` clean
- [x] Fixtures regenerated with `GOLDIE_UPDATE=true GOLDIE_TEMPLATE=true` so paths don't bake into snapshots

# Define UGCP constitution, canonical vocabulary, and cross-repo control semantics

This PR is the first step in converging the joint system into a true central distributed agent control plane.

## Context
Across `DannyFish-11/ufo-galaxy-realization-v2` and `DannyFish-11/ufo-galaxy-android`, the control core is partially converged, but core identities, session semantics, lifecycle vocabulary, and control terms still exist in parallel forms.

Examples include:
- `session_id`
- `runtime_session_id`
- `attached_session_id`
- task / execution / dispatch / delegated / handoff / mesh lifecycle states
- readiness / posture / coordination role / terminal reasons

This causes architectural drift: the system can appear distributed and coordinated, but still lacks a single stable language for a true central distributed control plane.

## Goal
Define the first formal UGCP constitution for the joint system and freeze a cross-repo canonical vocabulary covering:
- identity semantics
- session taxonomy
- control vocabulary
- lifecycle/phase vocabulary
- truth and authority terminology
- profile taxonomy

## Scope for `DannyFish-11/ufo-galaxy-realization-v2`
This PR should focus on the realization-v2 repository side of PR-1.

### Required outcomes
1. Add UGCP constitution and vocabulary documents, for example under `docs/ugcp/`.
2. Freeze canonical identity fields and session hierarchy for the control plane.
3. Freeze canonical control/state vocabulary.
4. Define a canonical phase graph and map existing lifecycle families into it.
5. Add cross-repo vocabulary alignment notes that explicitly describe how Android-side concepts should align with center-side semantics.
6. Ensure the documentation reflects the current authority-chain direction already present in the repo, without over-claiming implementation completeness.

### Suggested content
The documentation should explicitly cover at minimum:
- `task_id`
- `trace_id`
- `control_session_id`
- `runtime_session_id`
- `mesh_session_id`
- `source_node_id`
- `target_node_id`
- `execution_instance_id`
- `source_runtime_posture`
- `coordination_role`
- `dispatch_mode`
- `effective_mode`
- `delegated_signal_kind`
- `terminal_state`
- `terminal_reason`
- `readiness_verdict`
- `coordination_outcome`

The phase graph should clearly show how existing lifecycle families in the repo map into a canonical set of phases, including:
- ingress
- planning
- assignment
- execution
- transfer
- completion
- recovery

### Constraints
- Do not introduce misleading claims that the full protocol convergence is already implemented.
- Keep the documents grounded in the existing codebase and current architecture direction.
- Prefer adding clear, structured architecture docs and mapping tables over broad speculative refactors.

## Acceptance criteria
- The repository contains a UGCP constitution/vocabulary document set.
- The canonical identity/session vocabulary is clearly defined.
- The canonical control/state vocabulary is clearly defined.
- A canonical phase graph exists and maps current lifecycle families into it.
- There is an explicit alignment note for how Android-side vocabulary is expected to map to the center-side control-plane semantics.
- The PR is documentation-first and architecture-grounding oriented, suitable as the foundation for subsequent PRs in the plan.

   - 什么必须降级为 transport/adapter
   - 什么必须合并为统一 schema/state machine

author: alexjsteffen
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed is an injection vulnerability in the generation of FFmpeg concat list files (`ffmpeg_list.txt`). Filenames were previously interpolated directly into `file '{}'` lines.

⚠️ **Risk:** An attacker controlling a filename could inject newlines to add arbitrary FFmpeg directives or escape the single quotes to manipulate the `file` directive. This could potentially lead to unauthorized file reading or other unexpected behaviors when FFmpeg processes the list file.

🛡️ **Solution:** 
- Implemented `quote_ffmpeg_filename` to properly escape filenames by wrapping them in single quotes and using backslashes to escape any existing single quotes or backslashes within the name.
- Explicitly reject filenames containing `\n` or `\r` as they are invalid in the line-based FFmpeg concat format and pose an injection risk.
- Updated `combine_audio_files` to use this safe quoting function.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `src/main.rs`.

author: xjl010622
body:
## Motivation
When using `megatron_to_hf_mode == "bridge"`, the `AutoBridge.from_hf_pretrained()` method generates a model provider based strictly on the HuggingFace `config.json`. However, HF configurations only define the static model architecture and do not contain training-specific memory optimization arguments such as activation checkpointing (recompute).

Consequently, critical arguments like `recompute_granularity` are lost during the provider initialization. This causes activation checkpointing to fail silently, leading to unexpected and severe OOM (Out of Memory) errors during training, especially for large models or long context windows.

## Modifications
This PR explicitly synchronizes the recompute-related parameters from the command-line `args` to the `provider` before `provider.finalize()` is called. 

We use a safe iteration over `hasattr(args, ...)` to ensure compatibility even if certain recompute arguments are not passed in the specific launch script.

## Changed Code snippet (for review)
In `get_model_provider_func` (inside the `bridge` conditional branch):

author: gregmeyer
body:
## Summary

Closes the last finding from the original `/cso` audit: `data/secrets.enc` now encrypts under a passphrase-derived key (scrypt N=2^17, per-store random salt) instead of the v1 hostname+username seed. A stolen `secrets.enc` is no longer decryptable just by guessing the victim's hostname and username.

- New v2 payload format with `salt`, `kdfParams`, and an explicit `obfuscatedFallback` flag for users who choose the empty-passphrase legacy path. Readers honor whatever `kdfParams` the file specifies (bounded — defends against adversarial files that would OOM scrypt).
- `sua secrets migrate` re-encrypts v1 or obfuscated-fallback stores atomically via tempfile + rename.
- `sua doctor --security` reports the store's mode (`v2 passphrase-protected` / `v2 obfuscatedFallback` / `legacy v1`).
- `sua schedule start` preflights the passphrase requirement against each scheduled agent's declared secrets and refuses to start the daemon silently.
- `SUA_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE` env var is the CI/non-TTY escape hatch; setting it to the empty string is the explicit opt-in to the legacy hostname-derived fallback.
- Legacy v1 payloads still decrypt with a warning; next write auto-migrates.
- Instance-level derived-key cache collapses the read-then-write double-scrypt in `set`/`delete` to one derivation.

## Test plan

- [x] 269 unit tests pass (`npx vitest run`), up from 264 — 5 new cases for v2 round-trip, wrong-passphrase, env-var, empty-passphrase fallback, warn-once, v1 read, v1→v2 migration (both branches), KDF params round-trip + adversarial bounds validation, derived-key cache timing
- [x] Manual: cold store → passphrase prompt path writes v2 with `obfuscatedFallback` absent and 0o600 perms
- [x] Manual: seeded v1 store → `sua secrets migrate` under new passphrase decrypts and re-encrypts as v2
- [x] Manual: `SUA_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE='' sua secrets set KEY` → writes v2 with `obfuscatedFallback: true`, every read warns
- [x] Manual: wrong passphrase surfaces as a one-line `ui.fail` instead of a stack trace
- [x] Manual: `sua doctor --security` reflects passphrase-protected / hostname-obfuscated / legacy v1 correctly
- [x] Manual: `sua schedule start` with secrets-needing agent and no env var fails fast with actionable message
- [x] Manual: `sua agent run` with secrets-needing agent and no env var surfaces the clean error through the spinner

## Migration for existing users

```bash
# Option A: explicit
sua secrets migrate

# Option B: auto — the next `sua secrets set` or `sua secrets delete` migrates
sua secrets set ANY_KEY
```

CI: set `SUA_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE` in the environment. For the pre-v0.10 zero-friction behavior, set `SUA_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE=` (empty string) — preserved as a labeled legacy fallback.

author: houko
body:
## Summary
\`SECURITY.md\` promises \"Health redaction: Public endpoint returns minimal info; full diagnostics require auth\", but \`/api/status\` and \`/api/health/detail\` returned everything unconditionally. With the default \`api_listen = \"0.0.0.0:4545\"\` an unauthenticated LAN caller could read:

- every agent's UUID, name, running state, provider, and model (\`/api/status\` embeds the full \`agents\` array)
- \`api_listen\`, \`home_dir\`, \`log_level\`, \`network_enabled\`
- process RSS, uptime, session/active counts
- panic_count, restart_count, memory/embedding internals (\`/api/health/detail\`)

That's a free inventory of the target before the attacker has even picked a CVE.

## Fix
Redact both handlers in place (rather than touching the middleware allowlist, which is already under review in #2398). They now check the caller's \`Authorization: Bearer …\` against the live \`api_key_lock\` using a constant-time compare. Unauthenticated callers see only the same minimal \`{status, version}\` shape as \`/api/health\`, so probes / load balancers / orchestrators keep working. When \`api_key\` is empty (local dev mode) the full payload is preserved so local dashboards and \`librefang doctor\` are unaffected.

## Reproduction before fix
```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4545/api/status | jq '.agents | length, .home_dir, .api_listen'
# 11
# \"/Users/xiaomo/.librefang\"
# \"0.0.0.0:4545\"
```

After fix the same command returns \`{status, version}\` only unless a bearer token is supplied.

## Test plan
- [x] \`cargo check -p librefang-api\` — clean
- [x] \`cargo clippy -p librefang-api --all-targets -- -D warnings\` — clean
- [ ] CI full workspace build

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a small, maintainable CLI (`mdnsmap`) that discovers mDNS/DNS‑SD advertised assets and returns only records whose resolved IPs and service ports match operator-supplied CIDR and port filters. 
- Preserve full TXT key/value details for deep banner identification and optionally perform light HTTP/HTTPS enrichment for service banners without becoming a generic scanner. 

### Description
- Add CLI entrypoint `cmd/mdnsmap/main.go` exposing flags `--cidr`, `--ports`, `--iface`, `--wait`, `--timeout`, `--workers`, `--json`, `--output`, and `--verbose` and orchestrating discovery, filtering and optional HTTP enrichment. 
- Implement mDNS/DNS‑SD discovery in `internal/mdns` by invoking and parsing `avahi-browse` output into `model.ServiceRecord` entries and collecting raw PTR answers; records include instance name, service type/short name, host, port, TXT (raw + parsed + order), IPv4/IPv6 and TTL. 
- Add filtering and parsing primitives: `internal/filter` enforces CIDR matching while preserving non‑port identity services, and `internal/ports` parses/merges single ports and ranges. 
- Implement deep banner handling in `internal/banner` with complete TXT key/value parsing and ordering, plus lightweight HTTP/HTTPS probing that captures `path`, `status`, `Server`, `Content-Type` and HTML title when available. 
- Provide deterministic human-readable and JSON output in `internal/output` with stable sorting (by port, service type, instance) and a PTR answers section; add the data model in `internal/model`. 
- Add unit tests and fixtures under `internal/*_test.go` and a README documenting build/use and sample output. 

### Testing
- Ran unit tests with `go test ./...` and they passed for the implemented packages (`internal/banner`, `internal/filter`, `internal/mdns`, `internal/output`, `internal/ports`).
- Confirmed module builds with `go build ./...` successfully in the environment.
- Source files were formatted with `gofmt -w` prior to test/build to ensure basic formatting consistency.

author: alexdrgpy06
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The image processing command (`process_image_inner`) validated `out_path` against the Tauri `fs_scope`, but did not restrict the file extension. Additionally, the capabilities file granted overly permissive generic filesystem access (`"fs:allow-read"`, `"fs:allow-write"`).
🎯 Impact: Attackers or compromised frontend logic could supply arbitrary file extensions (e.g., `.sh`, `.exe`, `.bat`) to `image.save()`, allowing arbitrary file writes to disk.
🔧 Fix:
1. Implemented explicit file extension whitelisting (`.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.webp`) in `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` immediately after the scope check.
2. Scoped Tauri filesystem capabilities in `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` strictly to `$PICTURE/**` to enforce the Principle of Least Privilege.
3. Repositioned the inner `#![cfg_attr(...)]` macro in `src-tauri/src/main.rs` to fix a Rust compilation warning/error.
✅ Verification: Backend unit tests pass (`cargo test`), and the arbitrary write vector is closed. Frontend builds and tests function as expected.

author: copilot
body:
The Dockerfile refactor switched the base to `ghcr.io/slinkyproject/slurmd`, which is a compute-node-only image — it ships `slurmd` but not `slurmctld`. The startup script tried to launch both, causing `sbatch` to immediately fail with "Unable to contact slurm controller".

## Changes

**`docker/Dockerfile`**
- Add `slurmctld-source` stage from `ghcr.io/slinkyproject/slurmctld:${SLURM_TAG}` (mirrors the existing `sackd-source` pattern) and copy `/usr/sbin/slurmctld` into the final image
- Add `/var/lib/slurm/slurmctld` to the `mkdir` layer (required by slurmctld)

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/slinkyproject/slurmctld:${SLURM_TAG} AS slurmctld-source
...
COPY --from=slurmctld-source /usr/sbin/slurmctld /usr/sbin/slurmctld
```

**`docker/startup.sh`**
- Create `/run/munge` with correct ownership before starting `munged` (socket path required)
- Skip `mungekey` if `/etc/munge/munge.key` already exists — the base image ships a pre-generated key, and attempting to create another one errors out
- Add a readiness poll for `scontrol ping` after starting daemons to avoid a race where the sidecar starts before slurmctld is accepting connections; logs a warning if the 30 s deadline is exceeded
- Remove commented-out dead code

author: reshigan
body: ## Summary Fixes two bugs identified by Devin Review on PR #181 (photo review feature): 1. **Backend** — Both visit detail endpoints (`GET /visits/:id` at line 3092 and `GET /field-operations/visits/:visitId` at line 16936) now use `SELECT * FROM visit_photos` instead of an explicit column list. The original explicit SELECT didn't include `review_status` or `rejection_reason`, so the frontend's rejected-photo warning (`photos.some(p => p.review_status === 'rejected')`) was dead code — always `false`. Using `SELECT *` also avoids a regression where adding these columns to an explicit list would cause "no such column" errors for tenants that haven't run the review column migration, silently dropping **all** photos via the `.catch()` handler. 2. **Frontend** — `loadVisit()` moved from `try` to `finally` (guarded by `successCount > 0`). Previously, if a multi-photo upload partially failed, successfully uploaded photos wouldn't appear until manual page refresh. ### Updates since last revision - Switched from adding `review_status, rejection_reason` to the explicit column list → `SELECT *` instead. This matches the pattern already used by other `visit_photos` queries in the codebase (e.g. admin-review, photo timeline) and is safe for un-migrated tenants. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Migration still required for review workflow**: `SELECT *` won't break un-migrated tenants, but `review_status`/`rejection_reason` will simply be absent from results (returned as `undefined`). The admin approve/reject endpoints still require the migration (`POST /visit-photos/add-review-columns`) to function. Run it on all environments before testing the review workflow. - [ ] Test the rejected-photo warning by: rejecting a photo via the Admin Photo Review page → navigating to that visit's detail → confirming the red "Some photos were rejected" banner appears. - [ ] Test partial upload failure by: uploading 2+ photos where at least one is oversized or invalid → confirming the successfully uploaded photos appear immediately without manual refresh. ### Notes - Both visit detail endpoints were updated with the same `SELECT *` change. - The `.catch(() => ({ results: [] }))` on the `/visits/:id` query still means a truly broken `visit_photos` table returns zero photos rather than an error — this is pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this PR. - The frontend checks `review_status` via `(p: any)` cast — no compile-time guarantee if the field name changes. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/be8a6d400f604a07a4b8d1df301fb18c Requested by: @Reshigan ---

author: tejashchhatrala
body:
💡 **What:** Extracted the inline `[...Array(5)]` array allocations in `Testimonials.tsx` into a statically defined `STARS = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` array at the module level.
🎯 **Why:** To improve rendering performance. Previously, an array was dynamically constructed on every render cycle and during every iteration of the reviews map loop, creating unnecessary memory allocations and garbage collection pressure.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** While a formal JS benchmarking framework isn't established for this codebase, conceptually this change prevents `5 + 1 = 6` unnecessary array allocations per render cycle of the component. Micro-benchmarks for `[...Array(n)]` vs a static array map in V8 consistently show orders of magnitude faster execution and zero garbage collection overhead.

author: graylog-internal-actions-access[bot]
body:
Note: This is a backport of #25514 from `7.0` to `6.3`. Clean cherry-pick without changes.
Resolves #25259 

### Problem                                                                                                

`ClusterEventCleanupPeriodical` had a hardcoded cleanup period of **1 day** (86400s), regardless of the configured `max_event_age`. If `max_event_age` was set to e.g. 2 hours, stale cluster events could linger for up to ~25 hours before being cleaned up.

### Behavioral Changes

1. **Dynamic cleanup period based on `max_event_age`** — `getPeriodSeconds()` now returns the configured  `max_event_age` duration (in seconds) instead of a fixed 1-day interval, clamped to a minimum of **1 hour**  to prevent excessive DB load. Default is reduced to 12 hours given the performance impact noted by customers.

2. **MongoDB index reordering** (`ClusterEventPeriodical`) — The compound index changed from `(timestamp,  producer, consumers)` to `(consumers, timestamp)`. The `producer` field was removed since it's not used in the query predicate. This better matches the `eventsIterable()` query pattern, which filters on `consumers` (`$nin`) and sorts by `timestamp`. The new index allows MongoDB to satisfy both the filter and sort from a single index scan, whereas the old index order required scanning all timestamps first. **Given the 1-second polling frequency across all cluster nodes, the cumulative effect is substantial** — fewer documents scanned, no in-memory sorts, and a smaller index to maintain. On a cluster with N nodes, that's N queries/second against this collection, continuously. The improvement scales with both cluster size and event volume.
  
  3. **Joda-Time → java.time migration** — `ClusterEventCleanupPeriodical` now uses `java.time.Clock` / `Instant` / `Duration` instead of Joda's `DateTime`. The `Clock` is injected via constructor, making the class properly testable without global time mocking.

## Motivation and Context
Relates to #25259

### Manual test                                                                                         
                                         
  1. **Default behavior** — Start server with default config (no `max_event_age` set). Verify in logs that `ClusterEventCleanupPeriodical` schedules at 43200s (12h), not 86400s (1d).                            
                                                                                                          
  2. **Custom `max_event_age`** — Set `max_event_age = 1h` in `server.conf`, restart. Confirm cleanup schedules at 3600s.
                                                                                                          
  3. **Minimum clamp** — Set `max_event_age = 30m`, restart. Confirm cleanup still schedules at 3600s (1h minimum).
                                                                                                          
  4. **Index** — Check `db.cluster_events.getIndexes()` in MongoDB. Should show `{ consumers: 1, timestamp: 1 }` (not the old `{ timestamp: 1, producer: 1, consumers: 1 }`).
                                                                                                         
#### Smoke test
1. insert a stale event manually
```
  db.cluster_events.insertOne({                                                                           
    timestamp: NumberLong(0),                                                                             
    producer: "test",                                                                                     
    consumers: [],                                                                                        
    event_class: "java.lang.String",                                                                      
    payload: "test"                                                                                       
  })                                                                                                      
```             
2. restart with `max_event_age = 1h`, and confirm 
  - the event is deleted shortly after startup (`getInitialDelaySeconds()` returns 0).
  - this line is in the log:
> Starting [org.graylog2.events.ClusterEventCleanupPeriodical] periodical in [0s], polling every [3600s].

author: ntsrigaud
body:
Introduce the `RoleGuard` presentation component to conditionally display UI elements based on the authenticated user's role profile.

This component evaluates the active auth state against an allowed roles array, rendering the children on success, or a specified fallback node (defaulting to null) on failure. It safely handles loading and unauthenticated states without throwing errors.

This is strictly a display-layer utility for hiding restricted controls (e.g., administrative buttons or navigation links). Route-level security and access control remain exclusively enforced by the `ProtectedRoute` component.

Additionally, introduce a Vitest and Testing Library test suite for the `RoleGuard` component to validate conditional UI rendering based on authenticated user roles.

## Summary

Closes #67. Unifies celestial body position/rotation tracking into the arena-based `FrameTree`, replacing the flat `sources` vector and hardcoded `IntegrationFrame` enum.

- **FrameTree gains `reparent()`, `find_by_name()`, `is_descendant_of()`** — port of JEOD's `transplant_node()` for moving frames while preserving absolute state
- **Simulation owns a `FrameTree`** with root "Earth.inertial" — each gravity source gets inertial + optional pfix frame nodes, each body gets a frame node under its integration frame
- **Ephemeris updates sync into tree** — source positions/velocities and planet-fixed rotations update tree nodes each step
- **Sub-stage interpolation uses tree** — RK4 sub-stages interpolate source positions from tree base values, replacing the `time_frac` parameter
- **Frame switching uses `reparent()`** — replaces direct origin arithmetic with tree re-parenting that automatically recomputes relative state
- **`IntegrationFrame` enum removed** — frames now identified by `FrameId` (source index resolves to tree node)
- **`sources` vector removed** — gravity model data stored in parallel `GravityData` struct; position/rotation lives in tree nodes

author: nesquena-hermes
body:
## v0.50.35 — Cross-platform multi-workspace trust boundary

Fixes the over-restriction in v0.50.34 that blocked profile switching and all non-default workspaces.

**The problem:** v0.50.34 required all workspaces to be under `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE` (/home/hermes/workspace). Any profile with its own workspace directory (~/CodePath, ~/WebUI, ~/hermes-webui-public, etc.) got 400 errors on every session create or workspace switch.

**Three-layer model (Nathan's design input):**

1. **Blocklist** — `/etc`, `/usr`, `/var`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/boot`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/root` always rejected. Closes the original CVSS 8.8 path-pivoting vulnerability.
2. **Home-directory check** — any path under `Path.home()` is trusted. Cross-platform via Python's built-in `Path.home()`. Allows `~/CodePath` and `~/hermes-webui-public` simultaneously — no single-ancestor requirement.
3. **Saved-workspace escape hatch** — paths already in the saved workspace list are trusted regardless of location. Covers self-hosted setups with workspaces outside home.

**Verified against:** ~/CodePath ✓, ~/hermes-webui-public ✓, ~/WebUI ✓, ~/General ✓, ~/Camanji ✓, /etc ✗, /usr ✗, /var ✗, /root ✗, /tmp ✗

**Tests:** 1053 passed.

author: benoitc
body:
Adds a `stream_type_handler` option to `quic_h3:connect/3` and `quic_h3:start_server/3`. It's a function the H3 connection consults whenever it sees a unidirectional stream whose type it doesn't recognise. If the function returns `claim`, the H3 module hands the stream off to your code: you'll get `{quic_h3, Conn, {stream_type_open, uni, StreamId, VarintType}}` when it arrives, `{stream_type_data, uni, StreamId, Data, Fin}` for each chunk, and `{stream_type_closed, uni, StreamId}` on close. If it returns `ignore` (or you don't set the option), the bytes are discarded per RFC 9114 §6.2.3, same as #47.

This is enough to receive WebTransport `WT_STREAM` streams (varint type `0x54`). To send back on a claimed stream, use `quic_h3:get_quic_conn/1` and write directly against the QUIC connection.

Typical use:

```erlang
Claim = fun(uni, _StreamId, 16#54) -> claim; (_, _, _) -> ignore end,
{ok, _} = quic_h3:start_server(my_server, 4433, #{
    cert => Cert, key => Key,
    handler => fun my_http_handler/5,
    stream_type_handler => Claim
}).
```

Bidirectional streams still go straight to the HTTP/3 request path; deferring bidi classification to enable `WT_BIDI_SIGNAL` is tracked as a follow-up.

Four new eunit cases in `quic_h3_compliance_tests`; full gate green (1855 tests).

Base: `fix/h3-unknown-uni-stream-discard` (#47).

body: ### Overview This PR bundles UX/UI improvements, new filtering and sorting features, a community themes section, three new appearance toggles, player aesthetic refactoring, a server URL normalization bugfix, and i18n key consistency fixes across all supported locales. --- ### bugfix — Server URL normalization: silent streaming failure on trailing slash (`authStore.ts`) When users configured a Subsonic/Navidrome server URL ending with `/` (e.g. `https://server:4534/`), audio streaming URLs were built with a double slash (`//rest/stream.view`), causing playback to fail silently. Navigation (artists, albums, songs) worked correctly. The issue was particularly noticeable behind SSL proxies like Caddy. **Root cause:** `getBaseUrl()` in `authStore.ts` did not strip the trailing slash, while `restBaseFromUrl()` in `subsonic.ts` did. Streaming URLs (`buildStreamUrl`, `buildDownloadUrl`, `buildCoverArtUrl`) used `getBaseUrl()` directly. **Fix:** `getBaseUrl()` now strips the trailing slash, consistent with the rest of the codebase. ```diff - return server.url.startsWith('http') ? server.url : `http://${server.url}`; + const base = server.url.startsWith('http') ? server.url.replace(/\/$/, '') : `http://${server.url.replace(/\/$/, '')}`; + return base; ``` | User input | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `https://server:4534` | ✅ `https://server:4534/rest/...` | ✅ `https://server:4534/rest/...` | | `https://server:4534/` | ❌ `https://server:4534//rest/...` | ✅ `https://server:4534/rest/...` | | `server:4534` | ✅ `http://server:4534/rest/...` | ✅ `http://server:4534/rest/...` | **File:** `src/store/authStore.ts` ### feat — Settings: three new appearance toggles (`themeStore.ts`, `Settings.tsx`, `PlaylistDetail.tsx`) - **Cover Art Background** — blurred cover art as background in album and playlist headers; disable for solid theme background - **Playlist Cover Photo** — show/hide cover photo in playlist detail page headers; state in `enablePlaylistCoverPhoto` (`themeStore.ts`), applied conditionally in `PlaylistDetail.tsx` - **Show Bitrate** — shows bitrate (kbps) in the format column of song lists - Translation keys added in all 8 locales: `en, es, de, fr, nl, zh, ru, nb` ### feat — Settings: community themes - New **Community** section in the Themes settings page - Ships with 8 community-contributed themes: Amber Night, AMOLED Black Pure, Ice Blue, Midnight Blue, Monochrome Dark, Phosphor Green, Rose Dark, Sepia Dark - Designed as an open section — contributions from the community are welcome ### feat — Albums: advanced filters (`Albums.tsx`) - Z-A omitted — Subsonic API only supports ascending alphabetical order natively; local reversal would cause inconsistencies with paginated results. - Collapsible `Advanced` panel: dual-handle year range slider (1950–current) and track count presets: EP (≤4), Album (5–11), Double (≥12) - Client-side filtering via `useMemo` — no extra API calls - Visual indicator dot when filters are active ### feat — Favorites: filters, stats panel, and new columns (`Favorites.tsx`) - New columns: `album` (navigable link), `format` (MP3/FLAC/etc.) - Multi-select genre filter via `GenreFilterBar` - stats header: artists ranked by favorite count. Selecting an artist filters the list inline, showing only that artist's favorited tracks alongside an indicator displaying "showing X of Y favorites" - Year range filter applied to both favorite songs and albums - 3-state sort cycling on all sortable columns ### refactor — UI: modern-glass aesthetic & visual polish - Primary CTA button: liquid glass effect (specular highlight, inset shadow, micro-light 1px border, pill geometry) - Secondary controls (shuffle, queue) converted to low-opacity icon buttons - Album banner vignette: smooth gradient fade replaces hard crop between cover art and track list - Search input in `AlbumDetail` and `PlaylistDetail`: subtle background, magnifier icon, border on focus only - Removed redundant "Album" and "Playlist" pills from headers - Added Jetbrains Mono and Geist as variable fonts ### fix — i18n: key consistency across locales - `es.ts`: added 8 missing keys in `deviceSync` (legacy system) - `de.ts`: added 4 missing `cleanup` keys in `deviceSync` - `fr.ts`: removed 10 erroneous keys (Russian/Chinese/Dutch translations mixed into changelog); added 8 missing `deviceSync` keys - `ru.ts`: added 2 missing `player` keys: `lyricsSourceServer`, `lyricsSourceLrclib` - All 8 locales now have consistent, complete key sets for `deviceSync` and `player` --- > **Note:** Album type classification (Studio / Live / Compilation / Soundtrack) was not implemented — the Subsonic/OpenSubsonic API does not expose this field. Heuristic detection from album names would be error-prone; left for a future discussion before inclusion. ## Screenshoots ---

### Motivation
- Prevent misclassification of RJ45 10GbE ports as SFP+ and improve SFP family detection by using more explicit slot/entity hints. 
- Reduce false access-point/switch/gateway layout classification by improving model/hardware hint checks and using inferred port counts when available. 
- Improve special-port and port-index parsing to correctly detect `SFP28`, indexed SFP numbers, and only strip PoE when the layout defines a known PoE range.

### Description
- Added centralized `modelStartsWith`/prefix lists and used an `inferredPortCount` in `getDeviceLayout` to prefer gateway layouts for gateway-like models and to avoid incorrectly treating devices as APs when switch/gateway hints exist.

- Improved `detectSpecialPortKey` to identify `SFP28` and to distinguish `SFP+` vs `SFP` based on surrounding text (`translation_key`, `original_name`, etc.), and preserved existing WAN/uplink logic. 
- Added `_portMediaType` and related rendering changes (CSS class `media-...` and `is-sfp` logic) so UI rendering now distinguishes `rj45`, `sfp`, `sfp_plus`, and `sfp28` media types. 
- Tightened PoE stripping behavior in `mergePortsWithLayout` so PoE entities are removed only when the layout defines a known integer `poePortRange`.

Closes #1715.

Ships all five concrete `egg-checkpoint` CLI papercuts reported in the issue:

1. **`--checkpoint-repo` flag position** — accepted both before *and* after the subcommand via a shared parent parser.
2. **Silent empty results** — every "No checkpoints found…" path now prints `Searched <repo> branch <branch>` to stderr so the user knows where the tool looked.
3. **Composite BRC role names in `--agent-type`** — `reviewer_code`, `reviewer_contract`, `reviewer_agent_design`, `reviewer_refine`, `reviewer_plan` are accepted. Filtering collapses to `AgentType.REVIEWER` for the index lookup, then post-filters by the preserved `SessionMetadata.agent_role`. HTTP-path limitation documented in help.
4. **`--json` on empty** — every `--json` empty-result path now emits valid JSON (`[]` for list/browse/search; shape-matching empty object for context/cost) while the informational "Searched …" line still goes to stderr.
5. **Reviewer-checkpoint docs** — `--help` strings and module docstring note that reviewer agents may not produce checkpoints if session-end triggers don't fire.

All five fixes land in `shared/egg_contracts/checkpoint_cli.py`; `sandbox/egg_lib/checkpoint_cli.py` is a re-export so no additional edit is needed there.

body:
## Summary

D-012 from the vault/provider repair inch-worm backlog.

The optional `ouro up` AI-assisted diagnosis prompt still parsed acceptance with a raw `answer.toLowerCase() === "y"` style check, while the deterministic auth/vault repair prompts had already learned to accept `yes`, case variants, and surrounding whitespace. That meant the exact user habit we fixed for the deterministic prompts could still silently decline the next repair prompt.

This PR makes the repair prompt parsing DRY and consistent:

- exports the existing `isAffirmativeAnswer()` helper from `interactive-repair.ts`
- uses that helper in `runAgenticRepair()` for the AI-assisted diagnosis prompt
- keeps daemon CLI repair wiring mocks aligned with the shared helper export
- adds a focused regression test proving whitespace-padded `yes` accepts AI diagnosis
- bumps the alpha package versions and records the change in `changelog.json`

## Summary
This PR fixes a critical bug in `newrelic_log_parsing_rule` where invalid API credentials cause silent state file corruption. Previously, authentication errors during `terraform plan` or `apply` would remove the resource from state instead of failing with an error, requiring manual `terraform import` to recover. - Modified `getLogParsingRuleByID` to return properly typed `NotFound` errors

Resolves NR-548992

author: copilot
body:
CI was failing at `pip install` because `aku-platform-contracts` is a private GitHub repo and the runner had no credentials to clone it over HTTPS, causing git to attempt an interactive credential prompt that fails in a headless environment.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — Added a `git config` step before `pip install` that rewrites `https://github.com/` URLs to embed a PAT, enabling silent authentication:
  ```yaml
  - name: Configure git for private packages
    run: git config --global url."https://${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"
  ```
- **`requirements-dev.txt`** — Aligned `aku-platform-contracts` pin from `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1` to match `requirements.txt`

## Required manual step
Add a repo secret `GH_PAT` with a PAT (classic `repo` scope, or fine-grained scoped to `aku-platform-contracts`) under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**.

author: copilot
body:
Adds two new OTel metrics: an observable gauge for current queue depth and a histogram for message wait time (from which average time in queue is derived). Both are tagged with `queue.name` for per-queue filtering.

### New metrics

- **`bielupersistentqueues.queue.depth`** — `ObservableGauge<long>` reporting current message count per queue via `IMessageStore.GetMessageCount()` (O(1) in LMDB)
- **`bielupersistentqueues.message.time_in_queue`** — `Histogram<double>` (ms) recording `DateTime.UtcNow - message.SentAt` at dequeue time. Average time in queue is derived by the backend (e.g. Prometheus `rate(sum)/rate(count)`, plus p50/p95/p99 for free)

### Instrumentation points

- Queue depth gauge registered in `PersistentQueueOtelDecorator` constructor, iterates all queues from the store
- Time-in-queue recorded in all receive paths: `Receive`, `ReceiveBatch`, `ReceiveFromPartition`, `ReceiveBatchFromPartition`, `ReceiveFromPartitions`
- Uses `Math.Max(0, ...)` to clamp negative values from cross-node clock skew

### Files changed

- `MetricNames.cs` — new `QueueDepth` and `TimeInQueue` constants
- `QueueMetrics.cs` — `CreateQueueDepthGauge()` factory, `RecordTimeInQueue()` method, `_timeInQueueHistogram` field
- `PersistentQueueOtelDecorator.cs` — gauge registration + time-in-queue recording
- `PartitionedQueueOtelDecorator.cs` — time-in-queue recording in partition receive paths

author: hoverboardhavoc
body:
## Summary

Tested working with and without boost. Observed RPM increase at max throttle with boost enabled.

Enabling `BLDC_SINE_BOOSTER` fails to compile under gcc (PlatformIO toolchain) with:

```
Src/bldcSINE.c:450:28: error: initializer element is not constant
Src/bldcSINE.c:451:25: error: initializer element is not constant
```

Root cause: `uPwmBoost` and `uDiv24` are initialised at file scope from `BLDC_TIMER_MID_VALUE`, which expands to `(SystemCoreClock / 2u / PWM_FREQ)`. `SystemCoreClock` is a runtime variable from CMSIS, so gcc rejects it as a non-constant `const` file-scope initializer. Keil/IAR are more lenient.

Fix: drop `const`, leave the variables zero-initialised at file scope, and lazily compute on the first call to `bldc_get_pwm()`. No runtime behaviour change.

## Test plan

- [x] Builds cleanly with `BLDC_SINE_BOOSTER` defined (`pio run -e genericGD32F130C8`)
- [x] Builds cleanly with `BLDC_SINE_BOOSTER` undefined (regression check — booster block is `#elif`'d out)
- [x] Runtime behaviour verified on a 2.x.x board (untested by me — change is mechanical, just defers init by one ISR cycle)

- **New VBA Module**: `BaustellenAngebote.bas` with two main public procedures:
  - `NeueAngebotszeileEinfuegen()`: Inserts new offer rows starting from column I onwards, keeping columns A–H (cover sheet) stationary
  - `DatumsformatFixieren()`: Standardizes date column (I) formatting to `TT.MM.JJJJ` and auto-fits column width

- **Smart Row Insertion**: 
  - Prompts user for insertion row number and quantity via input dialogs
  - Only shifts data from column I onwards using `xlShiftDown`
  - Validates that insertions don't occur within header rows
  - Automatically applies date formatting after insertion

- **Date Handling**:
  - Converts text-based date entries (e.g., "14.04" or "02.03.2026") to proper date values
  - Supports partial dates ("DD.MM") using current year as fallback
  - Ensures minimum column width of 12 to prevent `########` display issues
  - Includes `TryParseDate()` helper function with error handling

- **Configuration**: Three private constants allow easy layout adjustments:
  - `INSERT_START_COL`: Column where insertion begins (default: "I")
  - `DATE_COL`: Date formatting target column (default: "I")
  - `HEADER_ROWS`: Number of header rows to protect (default: 1)

- **Documentation**: Added `README_VBA_INSTALLATION.md` with installation steps, usage instructions, and configuration guide

## Implementation Details

- Uses `Application.InputBox` for user interaction with type validation
- Implements screen updating optimization during row insertion
- Handles edge cases: empty cells, invalid dates, and column width constraints
- Follows German naming conventions matching the workbook's language

### Motivation
- Reduce chart noise by removing repeated swing/EMA signals and keeping only visuals required for entry (MR BSL/SSL, a single active FVG, first-take markers, and an entry arrow). 
- Replace sweep-every-swing logic with a strict first-liquidity-take policy after 09:30 to avoid label spam. 
- Ensure only one valid setup is active at a time and enforce a one-trade-per-side rule to prevent multiple same-side signals in a session. 
- Tighten the entry filter to require sweep → displacement+strict 3-candle FVG → first return into the same FVG with the first reaction candle as the entry lock.

### Description
- Replaced broad sweep/state machine with morning-range (MR) computation and first-take detection via `firstBslTaken` / `firstSslTaken`, triggered only after `09:30` and reset daily. 
- Added session-scoped gates `longTraded` / `shortTraded` to enforce the one-trade-per-side rule and prevent duplicate same-side entries. 
- Implemented single active FVG tracking with `activeBullFvg`, `fvgTop`, `fvgBottom`, and `fvgBar`, where each new valid FVG replaces any prior one and is cleared after the first touch (valid or invalid). 
- Simplified visuals and signal plotting by renaming the indicator to `ICT 2022 Engine CLEAN SIGNAL` and keeping only `BSL (MR High)`, `SSL (MR Low)`, `Active FVG` bounds, `First BSL/SSL Taken` markers, and `LONG/SHORT` entry arrows.

author: mihirchandna
body:
### Description
Apache Kafka added JDK 25 [support](https://kafka.apache.org/42/operations/java-version/) starting with version 4.2. Following that, we are updating CP-Ansible’s default Java version to JDK 25, replacing JDK 21

### Changes Made
**Default Version Update**
- Updated java package names to jdk 25 in `roles/common/defaults/main.yml`                     
- All existing molecule scenarios now run with JDK 25 by default via updated Dockerfiles.

**Ubuntu 20 JDK 25 Support**

Ubuntu 20 does not have `openjdk-25-jdk` available in apt repositories (maxes out at JDK 23). To handle this we used the same approach used for Debian 12 with JDK 21

- Created `Dockerfile-ubuntu2004-archive-java25.j2`, which downloads JDK 25 from the Adoptium Temurin API as a tarball to `/opt/jdk25` and Updated molecule files to use the new Dockerfile.
- Added a fail-fast gate for **Ubuntu 20 + `openjdk-25-jdk`**, matching the existing Debian 12 gate, so users get a clear error instead of 10 apt retry failures.

**Deprecated CLI Flag Fixes (CP 8.2 / Kafka 4.x)**

- `--broker-list` removed: Replaced with `--bootstrap-server` in `molecule/topic_data_creation.yml` (shared by 9+ replicator scenarios).
- `--producer.config` deprecated: Replaced with `--command-config` in `topic_data_creation.yml`.
- `--consumer.config` deprecated: Replaced with `--command-config` in: rbac-mds-kerberos-mtls-custom-rhel/verify.yml`

  The deprecation warning was being printed to stdout, corrupting audit log assertion checks.

The RHEL FIPS scnearios still fail because of https://confluentinc.atlassian.net/browse/ANSIENG-5843. The `security.useSystemPropertiesFile` that is used to Disable JVM level FIPS in ansible has been deprecated from JDK 25 and this needs to be updated with another appropriate property for FIPS

**Dockerfile Mismatch Fixes**                                                                                     
                                                                                                                

- Several scenarios had JDK 17 Dockerfiles but no java_package_name pin, meaning they ran the default JDK at runtime (JDK 21 on master, now JDK 25) on a mismatched Docker image. Updated Dockerfiles to match runtime JDK.

All molecule test run: https://semaphore.ci.confluent.io/jobs/f4bfeca0-5499-491e-a015-f3ba53b0ca9f/summary?report_id=63a7566e-bb24-3b6d-a18c-7af5cdce63f5 (re-run shows different failure addressed below)

### Motivation
- Enable scanning of learning-rate/step `beta` for `global_calib_AC_lr` and compare results with PT/SP validation while making minimal, surgical edits to analysis logic.
- Keep outputs separated per-beta and allow SP tests to use produced calibration files instead of hardcoded files to avoid mixing results across runs.

### Description
- Expose optional CLI parameters in `test/global_calib_AC_lr.cc` so a `beta` override and explicit input/output calibration file paths can be provided while preserving previous defaults. 
- Make `test/pt_test_AC_global.cc` accept an optional calibration input path and an output ROOT path, add a per-run `h_period` histogram and print `PT_PERIOD_SIGMA_NS` for easy automated summaries.

author: omar-z-z
body: This PR covers the complete frontend implementation of the Study Flow application, built with React and TypeScript. The app includes nine fully functional pages: Dashboard, Upload, Courses, Tasks, Progress, and Planner as the core study pages, alongside Login, Register, and Forgot Password pages for authentication. Each page is backed by a clean structure of custom hooks and TypeScript types organized in their respective directories. The authentication flow includes both the UI and logic layers. The Progress page features interactive statistics and live charts to visualize study activity. The app is fully responsive, with a burger menu for mobile navigation and a consistent top bar across views in the mobile view and a sidebar in the desktop view. A dark mode toggle is implemented globally, and the overall design is colorful and modern. Routing is handled via React App Routing with well-typed route definitions throughout.

body:
## [#77] orbit 라인 LineSystem 통합

### 변경 사항

`packages/core/src/scene/solar-system-scene.ts`:

- 궤도선을 `MeshBuilder.CreateLines` 9개 → `CreateLineSystem` 단일 mesh로 통합
- `createOrbitLine` 함수를 `sampleOrbitPoints`(점 샘플링만)로 분리
- `orbitLines: Mesh[]` → `orbitLines: LinesMesh | null` 단일 참조
- 가시성 토글은 단일 mesh의 `isVisible`로 일괄 제어

### 배경

P1 회고 기술 부채. P2-B에서 소천체/혜성/소행성대(N=100~1000) 추가 예정. 개별 Mesh 방식은 N에 비례해 draw call이 선형 증가 → LineSystem으로 단일 호출 상쇄.

### 스프린트 계약 (#77 DoD)

- [x] InstancedMesh 또는 LineSystem으로 통합 → **LineSystem 채택** (동일 색상이라 InstancedMesh보다 단순)
- [x] draw call before/after 기록 — **9 → 1** (9개 LinesMesh → 1 LineSystem with 9 batches)
- [ ] 시각적 회귀 없음 — 스크린샷 비교는 사용자 환경에서 `pnpm dev` 실행 후 확인 권장. 코드 레벨: 점 생성 로직 동일, 색상·가시성 동일

### 테스트

- [x] 89 단위 테스트 PASS
- [x] typecheck PASS
- [x] 한글 U+FFFD 없음

### 브라우저 3단계 검증

> 내부 렌더링 파이프라인 변경이라 3단계 모두 해당됨. 리뷰어/머지 전 로컬 확인 권장.

- [ ] **정적**: `pnpm dev` 후 8행성 궤도선 표시 확인 (색상 0.25,0.28,0.4 유지)
- [ ] **인터랙션**: 궤도선 토글 체크박스 (HUD 컨트롤) 동작 — 단일 mesh가 일괄 on/off
- [ ] **흐름**: 시간 재생/포커스 전환 시 궤도선 위치 유지

*CI 머지 후 로컬 검증 1회 권장. 의심 사항 있으면 이 PR에서 롤백 가능.*

body: ## Summary **SwapKit (api.swapkit.dev) confirmed malicious/phishing by Malwarebytes** — completely removed from entire codebase. All swap functionality now uses THORNode native API exclusively (no third-party intermediary, no API keys, direct protocol access). Deep adversarial audit rounds 6 and 7: **50+ bugs found and fixed** across all 29 Python files. Every file compiles cleanly. ## Critical: SwapKit Removal SwapKit was flagged as phishing by Malwarebytes Browser Guard. **All references removed:** - `SWAPKIT_API` constant — deleted from GhostSpiral and thor_swap_preparer - `--swapkit-api-key` CLI arg — deleted - `SWAPKIT_API_KEY` env var — deleted - SwapKit two-step flow code — deleted entirely - All URLs pointing to `api.swapkit.dev` — removed - SETUP.md, run launcher, requirements.txt — all cleaned **Replacement: THORNode Native API** - `GET {thornode}/thorchain/quote/swap` — no API key needed - 3 redundant endpoints: `thornode.ninerealms.com`, `thornode.thorswap.net`, `rpc.ninerealms.com` - Direct protocol access, no intermediary that can steal/log/block - Works in both GhostSpiral Stage 2 and standalone thor_swap_preparer ## Round 6 Bugs Fixed (BUG 115-145) ### CRITICAL (6) - **BUG 115**: `broadcast_signed_xmr` — undefined `rpc_url` variable (NameError on every broadcast) - **BUG 116**: GhostSpiral Stage 2 — only called /v3/quote, not /v3/swap (no deposit addresses) - **BUG 117-118**: `fake_leaf_inserter` and `label_poisoner` — missing `os` import (crash on every write) - **BUG 119**: `swap_retry_guard` — `before_sleep_log` ImportError (script can't start) - **BUG 120**: `testergatherSystem` — wrong `PBKDF2` import (should be `PBKDF2HMAC`) ### HIGH (8) - **BUG 121**: `swap_retry_guard` phantom failures advanced progress (money loss) - **BUG 123-124**: `testergatherSystem` clearnet aiohttp + socks5:// DNS leaks - **BUG 125**: PAG destructive log tampering (bash_history, syslog) - **BUG 126-127**: `dmswitch` name shadowing + randomized paths - Plus others (SML zombies, BTC_RE restriction, file permissions) ## Round 7 Bugs Fixed (BUG 146-150+) ### SwapKit Removal - Complete removal of all SwapKit code, URLs, CLI args, env vars - THORNode-only swap architecture ### OPSEC Hardening - `noise` — added `--onion-only` flag, clearnet exit warnings - `en_seeder` — removed env/CWD fingerprint from seed bundles - `vm_runtime` — replaced httpbin.org with check.torproject.org/api/ip - `testergatherSystem` — fixed MAC randomization, made numpy/Shamir optional - `paranoia_mode` — root-check warnings for privileged operations - `mirrormask` — re-implemented and wired up anti-forensics/decoy-injection/statistical-masking ### Module Fixes - `ghost_unifier` — docstring updated to match actual module names - `labelmask` — malformed DAG error handling added - `ghostmutator` — junk comment injection actually works now (8% probability) - `integrity_faker` — auto-created seed uses correct schema - `en_seeder` — removed brittle pickle serialization - `swap_retry_guard` — THORNode GET endpoints, phantom prob default 0 ### Documentation - SETUP.md — added Step 8 (stopping services), removed all SwapKit references - DEEP_AUDIT.md — full Round 7 documentation ## Files Modified (29) All 29 Python files + SETUP.md, requirements.txt, .gitignore, install.sh, AUDIT.md, DEEP_AUDIT.md ## Validation - All 29 files pass `py_compile` - All key tools pass `--help` - Zero SwapKit URLs remain in any executable code - THORNode endpoints verified reachable

author: andidev
body:
## Summary

Adds CLI flags on `paraglide-js compile` so more **`CompilerOptions`** fields that bundler plugins already expose can be set from the command line—especially **emit** toggles and **`isServer`**.

## Changes

### Emit output (parity with plugins)

- **`emitGitIgnore`**: `--emit-git-ignore` / `--no-emit-git-ignore` (default: on)
- **`emitPrettierIgnore`**: `--emit-prettier-ignore` / `--no-emit-prettier-ignore` (default: on)
- **`emitReadme`**: `--emit-readme` / `--no-emit-readme` (default: on)
- **`emitTsDeclarations`**: `--no-emit-ts-declarations` alongside existing `--emit-ts-declarations` (default: off)

### Runtime / tree-shaking

- **`isServer`**: `--is-server <expression>` — JavaScript expression emitted as `isServer` in generated `runtime.js` (default: `typeof window === 'undefined'` when omitted). Quote the value if it contains spaces, e.g. `--is-server 'typeof window === "undefined"'` or `--is-server 'import.meta.env.SSR'`.

Parsed values are passed through to `compile()` so normal runs and `--watch` stay consistent.

## Motivation

Bundler integrations already expose these options; the CLI did not, which made it harder to:

- Opt out of generated `.gitignore`, `.prettierignore`, or `README.md` in CI or scripts without the programmatic API.
- Control `.d.ts` emission and the `isServer` expression without calling `compile()` from code.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- Manual: `paraglide-js compile --help` lists the new options

Fixes https://github.com/opral/paraglide-js/issues/189#issuecomment-3519428715

author: houko
body:
## Why
Looking at recent open issues, four out of the most recent unlabeled batch (#2438, #2368, #2344, #2333) were going through with **zero** labels even though each one clearly belongs to an existing `area/*`. The current `issue-auto-label.yml` had three blind spots:

1. **Title-only matching, narrow keyword list.** It scans only the title, and only for `channel|kernel|runtime|sdk|security|docker|translat`. Issues mentioning `memory`, `api`, `mcp`, `provider`, `session`, `task`, `trigger`, `event`, `dashboard`, `cli` all slip through — even though `area/memory`, `area/api`, `area/cli`, `area/desktop` already exist in `labels.yml`.
2. **Conventional-commit prefix is the only path to a type label.** Bug reports almost never start with `fix:`, so they never get the `bug` label.
3. **`opened`-only trigger.** Reopened / edited issues never re-run, and there's no way to clean up historical orphans.

## What
- Extract the labelling rules to `.github/scripts/auto-label-issue.sh` so the same code drives both the event-driven path and the new backfill path.
- Scan **title AND body**, with `\b...\b` word-boundary regexes where the keyword is short enough to false-positive (`\bcli\b`, `\bapi\b`, `\bevent\b`, `\bauth\b`).
- Add patterns for `area/api`, `area/memory`, `area/cli`, `area/desktop`, plus `feishu`/`webhook` channels, `mcp`/`provider`/`prompt` runtime, and more conventional-commit prefixes (`perf`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`).
- Fall back to a new **`needs-triage`** label (added to `labels.yml`) when no rule matches, so orphan issues stay visible.
- Trigger on `[opened, reopened, edited]`.
- Add a `workflow_dispatch` input `backfill: true` that re-runs the labeller against every open issue currently missing labels — one-shot history cleanup plus a knob for future rule iterations.

## Smoke test
Ran the script locally against the four issues that motivated this PR:

| Issue | Title (truncated) | Old labels | New labels |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2438 | "Trigger event wiring: MemoryUpdate never emitted…" | — | `area/kernel` |
| #2368 | "Kimi/Moonshot provider: Rate limited after 3 retries…" | — | `area/runtime` |
| #2344 | "session_repair misses orphaned tool_use IDs…" | — | `area/kernel` |
| #2333 | "Emit Task Board events… expose TriggerPattern::Task*…" | — | `area/kernel` |

Plus a few synthetic cases:
- Random title with no signal → `needs-triage` ✓
- `feat: add a thing` → `enhancement` ✓
- `fix(channels): telegram polls leak` → `area/channels,bug` ✓

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge, `Label Sync` job picks up the new `needs-triage` label (or just runs `gh workflow run label-sync.yml`)
- [ ] Run `gh workflow run issue-auto-label.yml -f backfill=true` to backfill the historical orphans, then spot-check a few of the previously unlabeled issues to confirm they got area labels
- [ ] Open a fresh test issue with title `Test memory leak` and confirm it gets `area/memory` automatically
- [ ] Edit an existing issue's title and confirm the workflow re-runs and applies new labels

Initialization of non-lazy dependencies during registration introduces requirements regarding registration order, i.e., a non-lazy dependency can only depend on dependencies registered before.

By delaying eager (non-lazy) initialization until `ensureAllEagerResolved`, after all registrations are complete, this issue is resolved.

`DepsProvider` widget automatically calls `ensureAllEagerResolved` however, because `ensureAllEagerResolved` has to be async, there is no guarantee that async dependencies will be available with sync `get` in the tree below.

author: nyodas
body:
Add PodStatusBatchUpdates feature gate to debounce pod status writes

    Kubelet sends a PATCH /pods/status for every container state change,
    creating excessive API server calls and etcd revisions on multi-container
    pods. This adds a configurable debounce window (PodStatusUpdateBatchWindow)
    that coalesces rapid status changes into a single API call.

    Bypass conditions ensure critical transitions are never delayed:
    - PodReady changes in either direction (for endpoint controller)
    - Terminal phase transitions (Failed/Succeeded, for Job controller)
    - Force updates (deletion, termination)
    - Max coalesce cap at 3x window (prevents starvation)

    Alpha feature gate, default off. Default window 1s (range 250ms-5s).

author: benoitc
body:
Three commits landing datagram support for an external CONNECT-UDP library to build on.

The first two are RFC 9221 hardening. `do_send_datagram` used to only compare against the peer's advertised `max_datagram_frame_size` and would happily emit a UDP payload larger than the current PMTU; it now clamps to `min(peer_max, pmtu_budget)` and returns `{error, datagram_too_large_for_path}` distinct from the peer-cap error so callers can retry after PMTU grows. A new bounded receive queue (`datagram_recv_queue_len` option, default `infinity`) lets a proxy notice back-pressure via `quic:datagram_stats/1` without waiting for its mailbox to fill. PropEr properties cover roundtrips for both 0x30 and 0x31 shapes plus length-prefix coalescing.

The third commit is RFC 9297. Enable with `h3_datagram_enabled => true` on either side:

```erlang
{ok, _} = quic_h3:start_server(my_server, 4433, #{
    cert => Cert, key => Key,
    handler => fun my_http_handler/5,
    h3_datagram_enabled => true
}).

ok = quic_h3:send_datagram(Conn, StreamId, <<"ping">>).
```

The quarter-stream-id is added automatically. Owners receive `{quic_h3, Conn, {datagram, StreamId, Payload}}` on the request stream the peer framed against. Unknown stream ids are dropped silently per §5, and a peer advertising `SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM = 1` without a non-zero `max_datagram_frame_size` raises `H3_SETTINGS_ERROR` per §2.1. The underlying QUIC layer's `max_datagram_frame_size` defaults to 65535 when the H3 flag is on but the caller didn't set it explicitly.

CONNECT-UDP (RFC 9298) itself stays in a separate library as discussed — the Context ID layer goes on top of `send_datagram/3`. A capsule-protocol codec (RFC 9297 §3.2) is the natural next follow-up; not included here.

Full gate green on all three commits: fmt, compile, eunit (1869 tests), xref, dialyzer, `quic_datagram_e2e_SUITE` (12/12). Docs updated in `docs/HTTP3.md` and `docs/features.md`.

author: copilot
body:
Two residual architectural issues from the Final Integration & Cognitive Activation analysis: activation phase 7 reports incorrect status because `_orphan_streak` retains keys with value 0 for consumed signals, and `verify_and_reinforce()` relies on implicit defaults on first call.

### `CognitiveFeedbackBus.has_active_orphans()`

Added semantic helper that checks `any(v > 0 for v in self._orphan_streak.values())` instead of `len(_orphan_streak) == 0`. The old check always reported "incomplete" after any signal had ever been orphaned then consumed, since the key persists at value 0.

```python
# Before (buggy): dict has keys with value 0 → len > 0 → false "incomplete"
bus._orphan_streak = {'sig_a': 0, 'sig_b': 0}
len(bus._orphan_streak) == 0  # False — wrong

# After: checks actual streak values
bus.has_active_orphans()  # False — correct
```

Phase 7 status in `system_emergence_report()` updated to use the new helper.

### Cold-start bootstrap in `verify_and_reinforce()`

First call now explicitly seeds `mutual_verification_quality`, `uncertainty_metacognition_quality`, `root_cause_traceability_quality` at 0.5 baseline with a causal trace record. Guarded by `_cold_start_seeded` flag. Makes the initialization path causally transparent instead of relying on silent `read_signal` defaults.

### Tests

17 tests in `test_residual_fixes.py` covering helper correctness, phase 7 source-level verification, cold-start seeding, signal ecosystem integrity (267 bidirectional, 0 orphans), and version/phase-count regression guards. Existing 92 tests unaffected.

author: firecow
body:
## Problem

The `AlignMultilineParametersFixer` does not account for the `&` reference token in function parameters. For untyped reference parameters like `&$status`, the fixer treats `typeLength` as `0`, causing it to insert a newline between `&` and `$var`:

```php
// Before (correct input)
function test(
    GameRoom $gameRoom,
    &$status,
    &$statusCode
)

// After (broken output)
function test(
    GameRoom             $gameRoom,
    &
                         $status,
    &
                         $statusCode
)
```

## Fix

- Detect `&` before the variable name (or before `...` for variadic reference) in `getDeclarationAnalysis()`
- Include `&` in `typeLength` (1 char) so the alignment calculation works correctly
- Add `isReference` flag to the declaration analysis
- In unalign mode (`C_VARIABLES => false`), remove whitespace between `&` and `$var` instead of inserting a space

## Result

```php
// Aligned (C_VARIABLES => true)
function test(
    GameRoom $gameRoom,
    &        $status,
    &        $statusCode
)

// Unaligned (C_VARIABLES => false)
function test(
    GameRoom $gameRoom,
    &$status,
    &$statusCode
)
```

## Tests

Added 3 test cases:
- Untyped reference parameter (`&$b` with typed sibling)
- Multiple untyped reference parameters (`&$status`, `&$statusCode` with typed sibling)
- Mixed typed and untyped with reference

author: louistsai-csie
body:
## 🗒️ Description
<!-- Brief description of the changes introduced by this PR -->
<!-- Don't submit this PR if it could expose a mainnet bug, see SECURITY.md in the repo root for details -->

In the pre-allocation phase that deploys a contract, the framework supports passing in a dictionary that represents the storage to be initialized, and then embeds the logic inside the `initcode`. When the contract is created, it executes the initcode and performs the storage update.

However, in most of the benchmark cases, this is too inefficient, since the initialization phase requires a huge range of storage initialization, it leads to an `initcode prefix too long` issue.

### Solution

To resolve this issue, we create a helper for the stateful benchmark scenario. Users can define a storage init range like this:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StorageInitRange:
    """One contiguous range of storage to initialize."""

    start_slot: int
    num_slots: int
    offset: int
```

Which means the storage would be initialized to `STORAGE[i] = i + offset`, where `i` starts from `start_slot` to `start_slot + num_slots`.

We leverage the EIP-7702 authorization approach for testing. The workflow now becomes:

1. Delegate the authority to the storage initialization contract (`create_sequential_sstore_initializer`).
2. Initialize the specified range — this leverages `IteratingBytecode` with `transactions_by_iteration_counts`.
3. Pack the initialization transactions into blocks under the setup phase.
4. Re-delegate the authority to the real benchmarking execution code.
5. Start the BAL benchmarking phase.

### Design decisions

- The authority EOA is created in the BAL benchmark test, not inside the helper function. This provides the flexibility to use a stub account if needed.
- Nonces use `authority.nonce` (incremented in-place) rather than hardcoded constants, ensuring compatibility with execute-remote where nonces are fetched from the live network.
- Shared helpers (`build_sequential_storage_init`, `StorageInitRange`, etc.) live in `tests/benchmark/stateful/helpers.py` so they are reusable beyond the BAL tests.

author: dburkart
body:
Closes #162

## Summary
- Adds the RFC 0001 mmap-family syscalls at Linux numbers 9 / 10 / 11 / 28. `sys_mmap` supports anon-private and anon-shared; honours `MAP_FIXED`, `MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE` (EEXIST on overlap), `MAP_GROWSDOWN`, `MAP_STACK`; rejects file-backed fds with `ENODEV`. Exactly one of `MAP_PRIVATE`/`MAP_SHARED` is required.
- `sys_munmap` returns 0 on holes (POSIX) and splits straddling VMAs at sub-range boundaries. `sys_mprotect` gates with `range_fully_covered` so `ENOMEM` fires only when a sub-page is literally unmapped. `sys_madvise` implements `MADV_DONTNEED` on anon-private segments (drop PTEs + purge `AnonObject` cache) and no-ops the other standard advice values.
- Adds `validate_user_range` in `mem::pf` — the six-step canonical/alignment/overflow/USER_VA_END check the RFC specifies — plus `AddressSpace::range_overlaps_any` / `range_fully_covered` / `sys_munmap_range` / `sys_mprotect_range` / `sys_madvise_dontneed`. `VmObject` gains a default-no-op `evict_range` that `AnonObject` overrides to drop cache entries and release their refs.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo xtask build` compiles clean (pre-existing dead-code warning unrelated).
- [x] New integration test `kernel/tests/syscall_mmap_family.rs` drives `syscall_dispatch` directly and covers: fd!=-1→ENODEV, PRIVATE/SHARED validation, anon-shared round-trip, MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE overlap (EEXIST), MAP_FIXED silent evict, munmap on hole returns 0, munmap splits VMA middle, mprotect partial-VMA success, mprotect across hole returns ENOMEM, unknown prot bits EINVAL, MADV_DONTNEED re-zeroes, unknown advice EINVAL, musl-style malloc workload (16-page arena → free → 32-page regrow with zero-check).
- [x] `validate_user_range` has seven host unit tests in `pf.rs` covering zero-len, rounding overflow, non-canonical addr, addr+len overflow, alignment rules, round-down hint, and mappings ending exactly at `USER_VA_END`.
- [ ] CI will validate the QEMU integration tests on x86_64 (ARM64 dev container's x86_64 cross-objcopy is broken; local host run shows the kernel compiles without errors).

author: copilot
body:
This PR completes the remaining firmware-side scheduler integration for deterministic commit flow: completion wait is now IRQ-capable, the scheduler timebase is epoch-anchored to SYSREF, and validation now enforces minimum spacing for reinit-flagged events. It also aligns deterministic-path event payload construction and host coverage with these behaviors.

- **IRQ-driven `wait_done` path (with compile-time fallback)**
  - Added IRQ-mode wait flow in `awg_sched_wait_done()` behind `FMCDAC_AWG_SCHED_USE_IRQ`; retained polling fallback.
  - `awg_sched_arm()` now programs `IRQ_ENABLE` for `done|error`.
  - On completion, firmware reads `IRQ_STATUS`, stores it in `irq_status_latched`, then clears via W1C.
  - Added explicit IRQ bit definitions in register contract/header.

- **SYSREF epoch anchor support**
  - Added `awg_sched_set_epoch()`:
    - `TIME_RELOAD_LO/H I = 0`
    - `TIME_RELOAD_CTRL = 1` (load on next SYSREF)
    - polls `TIME_LO` until near-zero and emits `[SCHED-ARTIFACT] set_epoch ...`
  - Called from `fmcdac_run_scheduler_deterministic_path()` before loading events.

- **Validation rule: reinit spacing**
  - Added `AWG_EVTVAL_ERR_REINIT_SPACING`.
  - Extended validation rules with `min_reinit_delta_ticks` (default `8`, matching HDL minimum spacing intent).
  - Enforced spacing between `AWG_SCHED_FLAG_PHASE_REINIT` events.

- **Deterministic-path payload mapping cleanup**
  - Event construction now uses structured payload fields (`tone`, `freq_lsb16`, `scale`, `phase`) instead of opaque word literals.

- **Host test coverage updates**
  - Added IRQ progression test to simulate status/IRQ sequencing and exercise IRQ wait path.
  - Added reinit-spacing validation test for `AWG_EVTVAL_ERR_REINIT_SPACING`.
  - Introduced named constants in tests to avoid flag/IRQ magic numbers.

```c
ret = awg_sched_reg_write(AWG_SCHED_REG_IRQ_ENABLE,
			  AWG_SCHED_IRQ_DONE_BIT | AWG_SCHED_IRQ_ERROR_BIT);

ret = awg_sched_reg_read(AWG_SCHED_REG_IRQ_STATUS, &irq_status);
status.irq_status_latched = irq_status;
ret = awg_sched_reg_write(AWG_SCHED_REG_IRQ_STATUS, irq_status); /* W1C */
```

author: ifftu-dev
body:
feat(vc): PR 3 — DID layer (did:key + key registry)

Lands `did:key` self-resolution and the historical key registry that
PR 4's VC verifier needs. All 11 `crypto::did` unit tests and all 3
`tests/e2e_vc/did.rs` e2e tests previously marked
`#[ignore = "pending PR 3 — DID layer"]` now un-ignored and passing.

Implementation:
- derive_did_key / did_from_verifying_key — multicodec-varint 0xed01
  prefix + base58btc('z') multibase, per the W3C did:key spec.
- parse_did_key — validates `did:`, method = `key`, 'z' prefix,
  multicodec header, and 32-byte Ed25519 pubkey length. Distinct
  errors: UnsupportedMethod vs InvalidFormat.
- resolve_did_key — extracts the embedded VerifyingKey. No DB
  round-trip; did:key is self-resolving by construction.
- rotate_key — closes any open registry entry at `now`, inserts a
  new row, and (on first rotation for a DID) backfills a
  `valid_from = 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` row for the pre-rotation key
  derivable from the DID itself. This is what lets a verifier at t_v
  ≤ now still resolve the historical key — spec §5.3.
- resolve_key_at — picks the row whose `[valid_from, valid_until)`
  contains `at`, ordered DESC by valid_from.

Schema:
- Migration 022 adds `key_registry` with (did, key_id) PK, plus
  indexes on (did, valid_from) and a partial index on open rows.

Dependencies:
- bs58 0.5 — tiny base58btc codec. Every other option (multibase,
  multi-codec, pallas-crypto) pulled in heavier surface we don't need.

Design notes:
- `did:key` in a pure self-resolving sense only has one key per DID;
  the registry is what bridges did:key to rotation semantics. The
  `rotated_by` pointer on the closed row lets callers walk the
  rotation chain forward when they encounter a deprecated DID.
- The epoch-backfill is deliberate: it means a VC signed "before the
  registry existed" still verifies — which matches the spirit of §20
  (credentials remain verifiable even as infrastructure changes).

Verification:
- cargo fmt --check — clean
- cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings — clean
- cargo test --lib — 483 passed, 63 ignored, 0 failed
  (baseline 470/73/0 — 13 new unit tests passing, 10 un-ignored)
- cargo test --test e2e_vc — 3 passed, 34 ignored, 0 failed
  (baseline 0/37/0 — 3 e2e tests un-ignored)
